Authenticity has nothing to do with so-called reality. A story set in a world that could never exist could be absolutely authentic. Story arts do not distinguish between reality and the various nonrealities of fantasy, dream, and ideality. The creative intelligence of the writer merges all these into a unique yet convincing fictional reality.

真实性与所谓的现实无关。一个设定在根本不可能存在的世界中的故事，也可以是绝对真实的。故事艺术并不区分现实与各种非现实的领域，例如幻想、梦境和理想。作家的创造性智慧将所有这些融合在一起，创造出一个独特而又令人信服的虚构世界。

ALIEN: In the opening sequence the crew of an interstellar cargo ship awakes from its stasis chambers and gathers at the mess table. Dressed in work shirts and dungarees, they drink coffee and smoke cigarettes. On the table a toy bird bobs in a glass. Elsewhere, little collectibles of life clutter the living spaces. Plastic bugs hang from the ceiling, pinups and family photos are taped to the bulkhead. The crew talks—not about work or getting home—but about money. Is this unscheduled stop in their contract? Will the company pay bonuses for this extra duty?

异形：在开场片段中，一艘星际货船的船员从休眠舱中醒来，聚集在餐桌旁。他们穿着工作服和工装裤，喝着咖啡，抽着烟。桌上，一只玩具鸟在玻璃杯里漂浮着。其他地方，生活区里堆满了各种各样的小玩意儿。塑料昆虫挂在天花板上，性感女郎的照片和家庭合影贴在舱壁上。船员们谈论的不是工作或回家，而是钱。这次航行是否在合同的计划之内？公司会为这次额外的任务支付奖金吗？

Have you ever ridden in the cab of an eighteen-wheeler? How are they decorated? With the little collectibles of life: a plastic saint on the dashboard, blue ribbons won at a county fair, family photos, magazine clippings. Teamsters spend more time in their trucks than at home, so they take pieces of home on the road. And when they take a break, what’s the first topic of talk? Money—golden time, overtime, is this in our contract? Understanding this psychology, screenwriter Dan O’Bannon recreated it in subtle details, so as that the scene played, the audience surrendered, thinking: “Wonderful! They’re not spacemen like Buck Rogers or Flash Gordon. They’re truck drivers.”

你坐过十八轮大卡车的驾驶室吗？里面都有些什么装饰？摆满了生活中的小玩意儿：仪表盘上的塑料圣像、县集市上赢的蓝丝带、家庭照片、杂志剪报。卡车司机们待在卡车里的时间比待在家里的时间还长，所以他们把家里的点点滴滴都带到了路上。休息的时候，他们聊的第一个话题是什么？钱——加班费、黄金时段工资，这些都写在合同里了吗？编剧丹·奥班农深谙这种心理，他巧妙地用一些细节重现了这一幕，让观众在观看时不由自主地心想：“太棒了！他们不是像巴克·罗杰斯或闪电侠戈登那样的太空人，他们是卡车司机。”

In the next sequence, as Kane (John Hurt) investigates an alien growth, something springs out and smashes through the helmet of his space suit. Like a huge crab, the creature covers Kane’s face, its legs locked around his head. What’s worse, it’s forced a tube down his throat and into his belly, putting him in a coma. Science Officer Ash (Ian Holm) realizes he can’t pry the creature loose without ripping Kane’s face apart, so he decides to release the creature’s grip by severing its legs one at a time.

在接下来的场景中，凯恩（约翰·赫特饰）正在调查一个外星生物，突然一个东西跳了出来，撞破了他的宇航服头盔。这生物像一只巨大的螃蟹，盖住了凯恩的脸，它的腿紧紧地缠住了他的头。更糟糕的是，它还强行将一根管子塞进了凯恩的喉咙，一直通到他的腹部，使他陷入了昏迷。科学官阿什（伊恩·霍姆饰）意识到，如果不撕开凯恩的脸，就无法将这生物弄下来，于是他决定一根一根地砍断它的腿来解除它的束缚。

But as Ash applies a laser saw to the first leg, the flesh splits and out spits a viscous substance; a blistering “acid blood” that dissolves steel like sugar and eats a hole through the floor as big as a watermelon. The crew rushes to the deck below and looks up to see the acid eating through the ceiling, then burning a hole just as big through that floor. They rush down another deck and it’s eating through that ceiling and floor until three decks down the acid finally peters out. At this point, one thought passed through the audience: “These people are in deep shit.”

但当艾什用激光锯切割第一条腿时，血肉裂开，喷涌出一种粘稠的物质；一种灼热的“酸血”，它像溶解糖一样溶解钢铁，并在地板上烧出一个西瓜大小的洞。船员们冲到下层甲板，抬头看到酸液正在腐蚀天花板，然后在地板上烧出一个同样大的洞。他们又冲到下一层甲板，酸液继续腐蚀着天花板和地板，直到三层甲板之后，酸液才最终消失。此时，观众席上只有一个念头：“这些人麻烦大了。”

In other words, O’Bannon researched his alien. He asked himself, “What is the biology of my beast? How does it evolve? Feed? Grow? Reproduce? Does it have any weaknesses? What are its strengths?” Imagine the list of attributes O’Bannon must have concocted before seizing on “acid blood.” Imagine the many sources he may have explored. Perhaps he did an intense study of earth-bound parasitical insects, or remembered the eighth-century Anglo-Saxon epic Beowulf in which the blood of Grendel the water monster burns through the hero’s shield, or it came to him in a nightmare. Whether through investigation, imagination, or memory, O’Bannon’s alien is a stunning creation.

换句话说，奥班农对他的外星生物进行了深入研究。他问自己：“我的生物的生物学特性是什么？它如何进化？进食？生长？繁殖？它有什么弱点？它的优势又是什么？”想象一下，在最终确定“酸性血液”这个设定之前，奥班农究竟构思了多少种生物的特征。想象一下，他可能查阅了多少资料。或许他深入研究了地球上的寄生昆虫，或许想起了八世纪盎格鲁-撒克逊史诗《贝奥武夫》中水怪格伦德尔的血液灼穿英雄盾牌的情节，又或许这个灵感来自一场噩梦。无论奥班农的外星生物是通过研究、想象还是记忆创造出来的，它都是一个令人惊叹的杰作。

All the artists making ALIEN—writer, director, designers, actors—worked to the limit of their talents to create an authentic world. They knew that believability is the key to terror. Indeed, if the audience is to feel any emotion, it must believe. For when a film’s emotional load becomes too sad, too horrifying, even too funny, how do we try to escape? We say to ourselves: “It’s only a movie.” We deny its authenticity. But if the film’s of quality, the second we glance back at the screen, we’re grabbed by the throat and pulled right back into those emotions. We won’t escape until the film lets us out, which is what we paid our money for in the first place.

所有参与《异形》制作的艺术家——编剧、导演、设计师、演员——都竭尽全力，力求打造一个真实可信的世界。他们深知，可信度是恐怖的关键。的确，观众若想产生任何情感，就必须相信。因为当一部电影的情感负荷过重，变得过于悲伤、恐怖，甚至过于滑稽时，我们该如何逃避？我们会对自己说：“这只是一部电影。”我们会否认它的真实性。但如果这部电影足够优秀，那么当我们再次看向银幕的那一刻，就会被紧紧抓住，再次被拉回那些情感之中。只有当电影本身让我们得以解脱时，我们才能真正逃脱，而这正是我们当初花钱去看这部电影的初衷。

Authenticity depends on the “telling detail.” When we use a few selected details, the audience’s imagination supplies the rest, completing a credible whole. On the other hand, if the writer and director try too hard to be “real”—especially with sex and violence—the audience reaction is: “That’s not really real,” or “My God, that’s so real,” or “They’re not really fucking,” or “My God, they’re really fucking.” In either case, credibility shatters as the audience is yanked out of the story to notice the filmmaker’s technique. An audience believes as long as we don’t give them reason to doubt.

真实性取决于“关键细节”。当我们运用几个精心挑选的细节时，观众的想象力会补充其余部分，从而构成一个可信的整体。另一方面，如果编剧和导演过于刻意追求“真实”——尤其是在性和暴力方面——观众的反应可能是：“这不太真实”，或者“我的天，这也太真实了吧”，或者“他们不是真的在做爱”，或者“我的天，他们真的在做爱”。无论哪种情况，当观众被拉出故事去关注电影制作人的技巧时，可信度就会被摧毁。只要我们不给观众任何怀疑的理由，他们就会相信。

Beyond physical and social detail, we must also create emotional authenticity. Authorial research must pay off in believable character behavior. Beyond behavioral credibility, the story itself must persuade. From event to event, cause and effect must be convincing, logical. The art of story design lies in the fine adjustment of things both usual and unusual to things universal and archetypal. The writer whose knowledge of subject has taught him exactly what to stress and expand versus what to lay down quietly and subtly will stand out from the thousands of others who always hit the same note.

除了外在的生理和社会细节，我们还必须营造情感上的真实感。作者的研究必须体现在可信的人物行为上。除了行为上的可信度，故事本身也必须具有说服力。事件之间的因果关系必须令人信服且合乎逻辑。故事设计的艺术在于巧妙地将寻常与不寻常的事物与普遍性和原型性元素融合起来。一位作家如果对题材的理解能够让他精准地把握哪些内容需要着重强调和展开，哪些内容需要巧妙地淡化处理，那么他就能从成千上万个千篇一律的作家中脱颖而出。

Originality lies in the struggle for authenticity, not eccentricity. A personal style, in other words, cannot be achieved self-consciously. Rather, when your authorial knowledge of setting and character meets your personality, the choices you make and the arrangements you create out of this mass of material are unique to you. Your work becomes what you are, an original.

原创性在于追求真实，而非标新立异。换句话说，个人风格并非刻意为之。相反，当你对场景和人物的理解与你的个性相融合时，你从海量素材中做出的选择和安排便会成为你独一无二的作品。你的作品最终会成为你本人的写照，成为独一无二的作品。

Compare a Waldo Salt story (MIDNIGHT COWBOY, SERPICO) with an Alvin Sargent story (DOMINICK AND EUGENE, ORDINARY PEOPLE): one hard-edged, the other tender, one elliptical, the other linear, one ironic, the other compassionate. The unique story styles of each is the natural and spontaneous effect of an author mastering his subject in the never-ending battle against clichés.

比较一下沃尔多·索尔特的小说（《午夜牛郎》、《塞尔皮科》）和阿尔文·萨金特的小说（《多米尼克和尤金》、《普通人》）：一个风格冷峻，一个风格温柔；一个风格晦涩，一个风格直白；一个风格讽刺，一个风格充满同情。他们各自独特的叙事风格，是作者在与陈词滥调的永恒斗争中，对题材驾轻就熟的自然流露。

THE INCITING INCIDENT

诱发事件

Starting from any Premise at any point in the story’s chronology, our research feeds the invention of events, the events redirect research. We do not, in other words, necessarily design a story by beginning with its first major event. But at some point as you create your universe, you’ll face these questions: How do I set my story into action? Where do I place this crucial event?

从故事时间线上的任何一点，从任何前提出发，我们的研究会为事件的构思提供素材，而事件反过来又会引导研究方向。换句话说，我们并非一定要从第一个重大事件入手来设计故事。但在你构建故事世界的过程中，你迟早会面临这些问题：我该如何让故事展开？我应该把这个关键事件安排在哪里？

When an Inciting Incident occurs it must be a dynamic, fully developed event, not something static or vague. This, for example, is not an Inciting Incident: A college dropout lives off-campus near New York University. She wakes one morning and says: “I’m bored with my life. I think I’ll move to Los Angeles.” She packs her VW and motors west, but her change of address changes nothing of value in her life. She’s merely exporting her apathy from New York to California.

诱发事件必须是一个动态的、完整的事件，而不是静态的或模糊的。例如，以下情况就不是诱发事件：一个大学辍学生住在纽约大学附近的校外。一天早上醒来，她说道：“我厌倦了现在的生活。我想搬到洛杉矶去。”她收拾好她的大众汽车，一路向西，但她搬家并没有改变她生活中任何有价值的东西。她只不过是把她的冷漠从纽约带到了加州。

If, on the other hand, we notice that she’s created an ingenious kitchen wallpaper from hundreds of parking tickets, then a sudden POUNDING on the door brings the police, brandishing a felony warrant for ten thousand dollars in unpaid citations, and she flees down the fire escape, heading West—this could be an Inciting Incident. It has done what an Inciting Incident must do.

另一方面，如果我们发现她用数百张停车罚单巧妙地装饰了厨房，然后突然传来一阵猛烈的敲门声，警察拿着一张欠款一万美元的重罪逮捕令赶到现场，她则沿着防火梯逃往西部——这可能构成一起诱发事件。它已经达到了诱发事件必须达到的效果。

The INCITING INCIDENT radically upsets the balance of forces in the protagonist’s life.

导火索事件彻底打破了主人公生活中的力量平衡。

As a story begins, the protagonist is living a life that’s more or less in balance. He has successes and failures, ups and downs. Who doesn’t? But life is in relative control. Then, perhaps suddenly but in any case decisively, an event occurs that radically upsets its balance, swinging the value-charge of the protagonist’s reality either to the negative or to the positive.

故事伊始，主人公的生活大致平衡。他有成功也有失败，有起有落。谁不是如此呢？但生活总体上还是在他的掌控之中。然而，或许是突如其来，但无论如何都是决定性的，一件大事发生了，彻底打破了这种平衡，使主人公现实的价值取向要么转向负面，要么转向正面。

Negative: Our dropout reaches L.A., but she balks at taking a normal job when she’s asked for her social security number. Fearful that in a computerized world the Manhattan police will track her down through the Internal Revenue Service, what does she do? Go underground? Sell drugs? Turn to prostitution?

反面例子：我们的辍学生到了洛杉矶，但当被要求提供社保号码时，她却拒绝接受一份普通工作。她担心在这个信息高度发达的世界里，曼哈顿警方会通过国税局追踪到她，她该怎么办？遁入地下？贩毒？还是沦为妓女？

Positive: Perhaps the knock at the door is an heir hunter with news of a million-dollar fortune left by an anonymous relative. Suddenly rich, she’s under terrible pressure. With no more excuses for failure, she has a heart-thumping fear of screwing up this dream come true.

积极的一面：或许敲门声来自一位遗产继承人，他带来了一位匿名亲戚留下的百万美元遗产的消息。一夜暴富后，她承受着巨大的压力。再也没有失败的借口，她害怕自己会搞砸这梦想成真的机会，这种恐惧让她心跳加速。

In most cases, the Inciting Incident is a single event that either happens directly to the protagonist or is caused by the protagonist. Consequently, he’s immediately aware that life is out of balance for better or worse. When lovers first meet, this face-to-face event turns life, for the moment, to the positive. When Jeffrey abandons the security of his Davenport family for Hollywood, he knowingly puts himself at risk.

在大多数情况下，引发事件是指主人公直接经历或由主人公自身引发的单一事件。因此，主人公会立即意识到生活失去了平衡，无论好坏。当恋人初次相遇时，这种面对面的接触暂时改变了他们的命运，让他们的生活朝着积极的方向发展。当杰弗里为了好莱坞而放弃达文波特家族的庇护时，他明知自己身处险境。

Occasionally, an Inciting Incident needs two events: a setup and a payoff. JAWS: Setup, a shark eats a swimmer and her body washes onto the beach. Payoff, the sheriff (Roy Scheider) discovers the corpse. If the logic of an Inciting Incident requires a setup, the writer cannot delay the payoff—at least not for very long—and keep the protagonist ignorant of the fact that his life is out of balance. Imagine JAWS with this design: Shark eats girl, followed by sheriff goes bowling, gives out parking tickets, makes love to his wife, goes to PTA meeting, visits his sick mother… while the corpse rots on the beach. A story is not a sandwich of episodic slices of life between two halves of an Inciting Incident.

有时，一个引子需要两个事件：铺垫和高潮。《大白鲨》：铺垫，鲨鱼吞食了一名游泳者，尸体被冲上沙滩。高潮，警长（罗伊·施奈德饰）发现了尸体。如果引子的逻辑需要铺垫，那么编剧就不能拖延高潮——至少不能拖太久——也不能让主人公对生活失衡的事实浑然不觉。想象一下，如果《大白鲨》的剧情是这样的：鲨鱼吞食了女孩，然后警长去打保龄球、开停车罚单、和妻子亲热、参加家长会、探望生病的母亲……而尸体却在沙滩上腐烂。故事不是用引子前后两部分夹杂着零散的生活片段。

Consider the unfortunate design of THE RIVER: The film opens with the first half of an Inciting Incident: a businessman, Joe Wade (Scott Glenn) decides to build a dam across a river, knowing he’ll flood five farms in the process. One of these belongs to Tom and Mae Garvey (Mel Gibson and Sissy Spacek). No one, however, tells Tom or Mae. So for the next hundred minutes we watch: Tom plays baseball. Tom and Mae struggle to make the farm turn a profit, Tom goes to work in a factory caught up in a labor dispute, Mae breaks her arm in a tractor accident, Joe makes romantic passes at Mae, Mae goes to the factory to visit her husband who’s now a scab locked in the factory, a stressed-out Tom fails to get it up, Mae whispers a gentle word. Tom gets it up, and so on.

想想《河流》这部电影糟糕的剧情设计：影片以一个诱发事件的前半部分开场：商人乔·韦德（斯科特·格伦饰）决定在河上修建一座水坝，他明知此举会淹没五个农场。其中一个农场属于汤姆和梅·加维夫妇（梅尔·吉布森和茜茜·斯派塞克饰）。然而，没有人告诉汤姆和梅这件事。于是，接下来的100分钟里，我们看到：汤姆打棒球；汤姆和梅努力让农场盈利；汤姆去一家卷入劳资纠纷的工厂上班；梅在一次拖拉机事故中摔断了胳膊；乔对梅展开追求；梅去工厂探望被困在工厂里的丈夫（他现在成了工贼）；压力巨大的汤姆勃起困难；梅轻声说了些什么；汤姆恢复了性能力，等等等等。

Ten minutes from its end, the film delivers the second half of the Inciting Incident: Tom stumbles into Joe’s office, sees a model of the dam, and says, in effect: “If you build that dam, Joe, you’ll flood my farm.” Joe shrugs. Then, deus ex machina, it starts to rain and the river rises. Tom and his buddies get their bulldozers to shore up the levee; Joe gets his bulldozer and goons to tear down the levee. Tom and Joe have a bulldozer-to-bulldozer Mexican standoff. At this point, Joe steps back and declares that he didn’t want to build the dam in the first place. FADE OUT.

影片临近尾声十分钟时，引爆事件的后半部分上演：汤姆跌跌撞撞地走进乔的办公室，看到水坝的模型，便说道：“乔，你要是真建了那座水坝，我的农场就全淹了。”乔耸耸肩。然后，仿佛神来之笔，天降大雨，河水暴涨。汤姆和他的伙伴们开来推土机加固堤坝；乔则带着他的推土机和手下拆毁堤坝。汤姆和乔的推土机对峙起来，场面如同墨西哥式的僵持。这时，乔退后一步，声称他一开始就没打算建这座水坝。画面淡出。

The protagonist must react to the Inciting Incident.

主人公必须对引发事件做出反应。

Given the infinitely variable nature of protagonists, however, any reaction is possible. For example, how many Westerns began like this? Bad guys shoot up the town and kill the old marshal. Townspeople gather and go down to the livery stable, run by Matt, a retired gunslinger who’s sworn a sacred oath never to kill again. The mayor pleads: “Matt, you’ve got to pin on the badge and come to our aid. You’re the only one that can do it.” Matt replies: “No, no, I hung up my guns long ago.” “But, Matt,” begs the schoolmarm, “they killed your mother.” Matt toes the dirt and says: “Well… she was old and I guess her time had come.” He refuses to act, but that is a reaction.

然而，鉴于主人公性格千变万化，任何反应都有可能发生。例如，有多少西部片是这样开头的？坏人扫射小镇，杀死了老警长。镇民们聚集起来，来到马厩，马厩的主人是马特，一位退休的枪手，他发过神圣的誓言，永不再杀人。镇长恳求道：“马特，你必须佩戴警徽，来帮我们。只有你能做到。”马特回答说：“不，不，我早就把枪收起来了。”“可是，马特，”女教师恳求道，“他们杀了你的母亲。”马特跪在地上说：“唉……她年纪大了，我想她的时日到了。”他拒绝采取行动，但这本身就是一种反应。

The protagonist responds to the sudden negative or positive change in the balance of life in whatever way is appropriate to character and world. A refusal to act, however, cannot last for very long, even in the most passive protagonists of minimalist Nonplots. For we all wish some reasonable sovereignty over our existence, and if an event radically upsets our sense of equilibrium and control, what would we want? What does anyone, including our protagonist, want? To restore balance.

主人公会根据自身性格和所处世界，以符合自身特质的方式应对生活中突如其来的负面或正面变化。然而，即使是极简主义非情节作品中最被动的主人公，拒绝行动也无法持续太久。因为我们都渴望对自己的存在拥有某种程度的自主权，如果某个事件彻底打破了我们的平衡感和掌控感，我们会想要什么？包括主人公在内，任何人想要什么？答案是：恢复平衡。

Therefore, the Inciting Incident first throws the protagonist’s life out of balance, then arouses in him the desire to restore that balance. Out of this need—often quickly, occasionally with deliberation—the protagonist next conceives of an Object of Desire: something physical or situational or attitudinal that he feels he lacks or needs to put the ship of life on an even keel. Lastly, the Inciting Incident propels the protagonist into an active pursuit of this object or goal. And for many stories or genres this is sufficient: An event pitches the protagonist’s life out of kilter, arousing a conscious desire for something he feels will set things right, and he goes after it.

因此，诱发事件首先打破主人公生活的平衡，然后激发他恢复平衡的渴望。出于这种需要——通常迅速，有时经过深思熟虑——主人公接下来会构想出一个渴望之物：某种物质的、情境的或态度上的事物，他感到自己缺乏或需要它来使生活之舟保持平稳。最后，诱发事件推动主人公积极追求这个事物或目标。对于许多故事或类型而言，这已足够：一个事件打破了主人公生活的平衡，激发了他渴望某种能够拨乱反正之物的意识，然后他便去追求它。

But for those protagonists we tend to admire the most, the Inciting Incident arouses not only a conscious desire, but an unconscious one as well. These complex characters suffer intense inner battles because these two desires are in direct conflict with each other. No matter what the character consciously thinks he wants, the audience senses or realizes that deep inside he unconsciously wants the very opposite.

但对于我们最欣赏的那些主人公而言，引发事件不仅会唤起他们意识层面的欲望，也会唤起他们潜意识层面的欲望。这些复杂的人物会经历激烈的内心斗争，因为这两种欲望直接冲突。无论角色意识层面认为自己想要什么，观众都能感受到或意识到，在他内心深处，潜意识里渴望的恰恰是相反的东西。

CARNAL KNOWLEDGE: If we were to pull the protagonist Jonathan (Jack Nicholson) aside and ask him “What do you want?” his conscious answer would be: “I’m a good-looking guy, lot of fun to be with, make a terrific living as a CPA. My life would be paradise if I could find the perfect woman to share it.” The film takes Jonathan from his college years to middle age, a thirty-year search for his dream woman. Again and again he meets a beautiful, intelligent woman, but soon their candlelit romance turns to dark emotions, acts of physical violence, then breakup. Over and over he plays the great romantic until he has a woman head over heels in love with him, then he turns on her, humiliates her, and hurls her out of his life.

肉体知识：如果我们把主人公乔纳森（杰克·尼科尔森饰）拉到一边，问他“你想要什么？”，他理智上的回答会是：“我长相英俊，风趣幽默，作为一名注册会计师收入颇丰。如果能找到一个完美的女人与我共度余生，我的生活就如同天堂。”这部电影讲述了乔纳森从大学时代到中年，三十年来寻找梦中情人的历程。他一次又一次地遇到美丽聪慧的女子，但很快，他们烛光下的浪漫情愫便会演变成阴暗的情绪、肢体暴力，最终走向分手。他一次又一次地扮演浪漫情圣，直到一个女人对他神魂颠倒，然后他又会背叛她，羞辱她，并将她彻底抛弃。

At Climax, he invites Sandy (Art Garfunkel), an old college buddy, for dinner. For amusement he screens 35mm slides of all the women from his life; a show he entitles “Ballbusters on Parade.” As each woman appears, he trashes her to Sandy for “what was wrong with her.” In the Resolution scene, he’s with a prostitute (Rita Moreno) who has to read him an ode he’s written in praise of his penis so he can get it up. He thinks he’s hunting for the perfect woman, but we know that unconsciously he wants to degrade and destroy women and has done that throughout his life. Jules Feiffer’s screenplay is a chilling delineation of a man that too many women know only too well.

在“高潮”餐厅，他邀请老同学桑迪（阿特·加芬克尔饰）共进晚餐。为了消遣，他放映了自己生命中所有女性的35毫米幻灯片，并将其命名为“坏女人游行”。每当一个女人出现，他都会向桑迪贬低她，质问她“到底哪里不好”。在“结局”那场戏中，他和一个妓女（丽塔·莫雷诺饰）在一起，妓女必须朗读他自己写的一首赞美自己阴茎的颂歌，才能让他勃起。他以为自己在寻找完美女人，但我们知道，他潜意识里渴望贬低和摧毁女性，而且他一生都在这样做。朱尔斯·费弗的剧本对这样一个男人进行了令人不寒而栗的刻画，而太多女性对此都感同身受。

MRS. SOFFEL: In 1901 a thief (Mel Gibson) who’s committed murder awaits execution. The wife of the prison warden (Diane Keaton) decides to save his soul for God. She reads Bible quotations to him, hoping that when he’s hanged he’ll go to heaven and not hell. They are attracted. She engineers his jailbreak, then joins him. On the run they make love, but only once. As the authorities close in, she realizes he’s about to die and decides to die with him: “Shoot me,” she begs him, “I don’t want to live a day beyond you.” He pulls the trigger but only wounds her. In the Resolution, she’s imprisoned for life, but goes into her cell proudly, virtually spitting in the eye of her jailer.

索菲尔夫人：1901年，一名犯下谋杀罪的窃贼（梅尔·吉布森饰）即将被处决。监狱长的妻子（黛安·基顿饰）决定拯救他的灵魂，让他回归上帝。她为他朗读圣经经文，希望他被绞死后能升入天堂而不是地狱。两人彼此吸引。她策划了他的越狱，然后与他一同逃亡。在逃亡途中，他们发生了关系，但仅此一次。当当局步步逼近时，她意识到他即将被处死，决定与他同归于尽：“开枪打死我吧，”她哀求道，“我不想在你之后活过一天。”他扣动了扳机，却只伤到了她。在最终的结局中，她被判终身监禁，但她昂首挺胸地走进牢房，几乎是在对狱卒吐口水。

Mrs. Soffel seems to flit from choice to choice, but we sense that underneath her changes of mind is the powerful unconscious desire for a transcendent, absolute, romantic experience of such intensity that if nothing ever happened to her again it wouldn’t matter… because for one sublime moment she will have lived. Mrs. Soffel is the ultimate romantic.

索菲尔太太似乎总是摇摆不定，但我们能感觉到，在她反复无常的内心深处，隐藏着一种强烈的、无意识的渴望：她渴望体验一种超凡脱俗、绝对纯粹的浪漫，那种体验如此强烈，以至于即便她此后再无其他经历，也无关紧要……因为在那崇高的瞬间，她已然活过。索菲尔太太，是终极的浪漫主义者。

THE CRYING GAME: Fergus (Stephen Rea), a member of the Irish Republican Army, is put in charge of a British corporal (Forest Whitaker) held prisoner by his IRA unit. He finds himself in sympathy with the man’s plight. When the corporal is killed, Fergus goes AWOL to England, hiding out from both the British and the IRA. He looks up the corporal’s lover, Dil (Jaye Davidson). He falls in love, only to discover that Dil’s a transvestite. The IRA then tracks him down. Fergus volunteered for the IRA knowing it isn’t a college fraternity, so when they order him to assassinate an English judge, he must finally come to terms with his politics. Is he or is he not an Irish patriot?

《哭泣的游戏》：爱尔兰共和军成员弗格斯（斯蒂芬·雷饰）被指派负责看管一名被他所在爱尔兰共和军小队俘虏的英国下士（福里斯特·惠特克饰）。他发现自己对这名下士的困境深表同情。下士阵亡后，弗格斯擅离职守逃往英国，躲避英国和爱尔兰共和军的追捕。他找到了下士的情人迪尔（杰伊·戴维森饰），并坠入爱河，却发现迪尔是一名异装癖者。爱尔兰共和军随后追踪到了他。弗格斯自愿加入爱尔兰共和军，因为他知道这并非大学兄弟会，所以当他们命令他刺杀一名英国法官时，他最终必须面对自己的政治立场。他究竟是不是一位爱尔兰爱国者？

Beneath Fergus’s conscious political struggle, the audience senses from his first moments with the prisoner to his last tender scenes with Dil that this film isn’t about his commitment to the cause. Hidden behind his zigzag politics Fergus harbors the most human of needs: to love and be loved.

在弗格斯自觉的政治斗争背后，从他与囚犯的初次相遇到与迪尔的最后温情戏份，观众都能感受到这部电影并非着重展现他对事业的忠诚。在他摇摆不定的政治立场背后，弗格斯内心深处藏着最基本的人性需求：爱与被爱。

THE SPINE OF THE STORY

故事的主线

The energy of a protagonist’s desire forms the critical element of design known as the Spine of the story (AKA Through-line or Super-objective ). The Spine is the deep desire in and effort by the protagonist to restore the balance of life. It’s the primary unifying force that holds all other story elements together. For no matter what happens on the surface of the story, each scene, image, and word is ultimately an aspect of the Spine, relating, causally or thematically, to this core of desire and action.

主人公的渴望能量构成了故事设计中至关重要的元素，即故事的主线（又称贯穿线或超目标）。主线是主人公内心深处渴望并努力恢复生活平衡的愿望，也是将所有其他故事元素凝聚在一起的主要统一力量。因为无论故事表面如何发展，每一个场景、画面和文字最终都是主线的一个方面，它们在因果关系或主题上都与这一核心的渴望和行动息息相关。

If the protagonist has no unconscious desire, then his conscious objective becomes the Spine. The Spine of any Bond film, for example, can be phrased as: To defeat the arch-villain. James has no unconscious desires; he wants and only wants to save the world. As the story’s unifying force, Bond’s pursuit of his conscious goal cannot change. If he were to declare, “To hell with Dr. No. I’m bored with the spy business. I’m going south to work on my back-swing and lower my handicap,” the film falls apart.

如果主角没有潜意识的欲望，那么他有意识的目标就成了故事的脊梁。例如，任何一部邦德电影的脊梁都可以概括为：打败大反派。詹姆斯没有潜意识的欲望；他想要，也只有拯救世界这一件事。作为故事的统一力量，邦德对自身目标的追求是不可改变的。如果他突然宣布：“去他的诺博士！我对间谍活动感到厌倦了。我要去南方练练挥杆，降低我的差点！”那么这部电影就彻底崩塌了。

If, on the other hand, the protagonist has an unconscious desire, this becomes the Spine of the story. An unconscious desire is always more powerful and durable, with roots reaching to the protagonist’s innermost self. When an unconscious desire drives the story, it allows the writer to create a far more complex character who may repeatedly change his conscious desire.

另一方面，如果主人公拥有潜意识中的欲望，那么这便成为故事的脊梁。潜意识中的欲望总是更加强大持久，其根源直达主人公的内心深处。当潜意识中的欲望驱动故事发展时，作者便能塑造出一个更为复杂的人物，这个人物的意识欲望可能会反复变化。

MOBY DICK: If Melville had made Ahab sole protagonist, his novel would be a simple but exciting work of High Adventure , driven by the captain’s monomania to destroy the white whale. But by adding Ishmael as dual protagonist, Melville enriched his story into a complex classic of the Education Plot. For the telling is in fact driven by Ishmael’s unconscious desire to battle inner demons, seeking in himself the destructive obsessions he sees in Ahab—a desire that not only contradicts his conscious hope to survive Ahab’s mad voyage, but may destroy him as it does Ahab.

《白鲸》：如果梅尔维尔只让亚哈船长作为唯一的主角，那么这部小说就会是一部情节简单却引人入胜的冒险故事，其核心在于船长一心想要杀死白鲸的执念。但通过引入以实玛利作为双主角，梅尔维尔将故事丰富成了一部复杂而经典的教育叙事作品。因为故事的叙述实际上是由以实玛利潜意识中与内心恶魔搏斗的渴望所驱动的，他试图在自己身上找到亚哈身上那种毁灭性的执念——这种渴望不仅与他清醒时想要在亚哈疯狂的航行中幸存下来的愿望相悖，而且很可能像毁灭亚哈一样毁灭他自己。

In THE CRYING GAME Fergus agonizes over politics while his unconscious need to love and be loved drives the telling. Jonathan searches for the “perfect woman” in CARNAL KNOWLEDGE, flitting from relationship to relationship, while his unconscious desire to humiliate and destroy women never varies. The leaps of desire in Mrs. Soffel’s mind are enormous—from salvation to damnation—while unconsciously she seeks to experience the transcendent romance. The audience senses that the shifting urges of the complex protagonist are merely reflections of the one thing that never changes: the unconscious desire.

在《哭泣的游戏》中，弗格斯为政治问题苦恼不已，而他潜意识里渴望爱与被爱的欲望却驱动着故事的展开。在《肉体知识》中，乔纳森苦苦寻觅“完美女人”，在一段又一段感情中摇摆不定，而他潜意识里羞辱和摧毁女性的欲望却始终如一。索菲尔太太的欲望在她心中经历了巨大的飞跃——从救赎到堕落——而她潜意识里却渴望体验那种超凡脱俗的浪漫。观众会意识到，这些复杂主人公不断变化的欲望，只不过是反映了一个永恒不变的本质：潜意识里的欲望。

THE QUEST

探索

From the point of view of the writer looking from the Inciting Incident “down the Spine” to the last act’s Climax, in spite of all we’ve said about genres and the various shapes from Archplot to Antiplot, in truth there’s only one story. In essence we have told one another the same tale, one way or another, since the dawn of humanity, and that story could be usefully called the Quest. All stories take the form of a Quest.

从作者的视角出发，沿着故事主线，从最初的导火索一路向下，直至最终的高潮，尽管我们讨论了各种类型以及从主线剧情到反主线剧情的各种形式，但实际上，故事只有一个。自人类文明伊始，我们便以各种方式讲述着同一个故事，而这个故事可以恰当地称为“探寻”。所有故事都以探寻的形式呈现。

For better or worse, an event throws a character’s life out of balance, arousing in him the conscious and/or unconscious desire for that which he feels will restore balance, launching him on a Quest for his Object of Desire against forces of antagonism (inner, personal, extra-personal). He may or may not achieve it. This is story in a nutshell.

无论好坏，某个事件都会打破角色生活的平衡，唤起他内心深处对某种事物的渴望——他认为这种事物能够恢复平衡——从而开启一段寻找渴望之物的旅程，而他需要对抗各种阻力（内在的、个人的、外在的）。他最终能否成功，则不得而知。这就是故事的精髓所在。

The essential form of story is simple. But that’s like saying that the essential form of music is simple. It is. It’s twelve notes. But these twelve notes conspire into everything and anything we have ever called music. The essential elements of the Quest are the twelve notes of our music, the melody we’ve listened to all our lives. However, like the composer sitting down at the piano, when a writer takes up this seemingly simple form, he discovers how incredibly complex it is, how inordinately difficult to do.

故事的本质形式很简单。但这就像说音乐的本质形式也很简单一样。的确很简单，它由十二个音符构成。但这十二个音符构成了我们称之为音乐的一切。探索之旅的本质元素就是我们音乐中的十二个音符，是我们一生都在聆听的旋律。然而，就像作曲家坐在钢琴前一样，当作家采用这种看似简单的形式时，他会发现它是多么复杂，多么难以驾驭。

To understand the Quest form of your story you need only identify your protagonist’s Object of Desire. Penetrate his psychology and find an honest answer to the question: “What does he want?” It may be the desire for something he can take into his arms: someone to love in MOONSTRUCK. It may be the need for inner growth: maturity in BIG. But whether a profound change in the real world— security from a marauding shark in JAWS—or a profound change in the spiritual realm— a meaningful life in TENDER MERCIES—by looking into the heart of the protagonist and discovering his desire, you begin to see the arc of your story, the Quest on which the Inciting Incident sends him.

要理解你故事中的“探寻”结构，你只需确定主人公的渴望对象。深入他的心理，找到“他想要什么？”这个问题的真诚答案。这或许是渴望拥有可以拥抱的东西：比如《月色撩人》中的爱人。或许是渴望内心成长：比如《长大成人》中的成熟。但无论是现实世界的深刻改变——比如《大白鲨》中免受鲨鱼袭击的安全感——还是精神领域的深刻转变——比如《温柔的怜悯》中有意义的人生——通过审视主人公的内心，发现他的渴望，你就能开始看到故事的弧线，以及引发事件所引导他踏上的探寻之旅。

DESIGN OF THE INCITING INCIDENT

引发事件的设计

An Inciting Incident happens in only one of two ways: randomly or causally, either by coincidence or by decision. If by decision, it can be made by the protagonist—Ben’s decision to drink himself to death in LEAVING LAS VEGAS, or, as in KRAMER vs. KRAMER, by someone with the power to upset the protagonist’s life—Mrs. Kramer’s decision to leave Mr. Kramer and their child. If by coincidence, it may be tragic—the accident that kills Alice’s husband in ALICE DOESN’T LIVE HERE ANYMORE, or serendipitous—a sports promoter meets beautiful and gifted athlete in PAT AND MIKE. By choice or accident; there are no other means.

引发事件的发生只有两种方式：随机或因果，要么是巧合，要么是人为决定。如果是人为决定，可能是主人公自己做出的——比如《离开拉斯维加斯》中本决定酗酒致死，或者像《克莱默夫妇》中那样，由有能力扰乱主人公生活的人做出——比如克莱默太太决定离开克莱默先生和他们的孩子。如果是巧合，可能是悲剧性的——比如《爱丽丝不再住在这里》中爱丽丝丈夫的意外身亡，也可能是偶然的——比如《帕特和迈克》中体育推广人邂逅美丽又有天赋的运动员。要么是选择，要么是意外；没有其他方式。

The Inciting Incident of the Central Plot must happen onscreen—not in the Backstory, not between scenes offscreen. Each subplot has its own Inciting Incident, which may or may not be onscreen, but the presence of the audience at the Central Plot’s Inciting Incident is crucial to story design for two reasons.

中心情节的诱发事件必须发生在屏幕上——而不是在背景故事中，也不是在幕后场景之间。每个子情节都有自己的诱发事件，这些事件可能发生在屏幕上，也可能不发生在屏幕上，但观众在中心情节诱发事件发生时在场对于故事设计至关重要，原因有二。

First, when the audience experiences an Inciting Incident, the film’s Major Dramatic Question, a variation on “How will this turn out?” is provoked to mind. JAWS: Will the sheriff kill the shark, or the shark the sheriff? LA NOTTE: After Lidia (Jeanne Moreau) tells her husband (Marcello Mastroianni) that he disgusts her and she’s leaving, will she go or stay? JALSAGHER (THE MUSIC ROOM): Biswas (Huzur Roy), an aristocrat with a life-consuming love of music, decides to sell his wife’s jewels, then his palace to finance his passion for beauty. Will extravagance destroy or redeem this connoisseur?

首先，当观众经历一个引发事件，也就是影片的主要戏剧性问题时，脑海中会浮现出“事情会如何发展？”这样的疑问。《大白鲨》：警长会杀死鲨鱼，还是鲨鱼会杀死警长？《夜》：莉迪亚（让娜·莫罗饰）告诉丈夫（马塞洛·马斯楚安尼饰）她厌恶他，要离开，她会走还是会留下？《音乐室》：比斯瓦斯（胡祖尔·罗伊饰）是一位痴迷音乐的贵族，他决定卖掉妻子的珠宝，然后卖掉自己的宫殿，来资助他对美的追求。奢靡之风会毁灭还是救赎这位鉴赏家？

In Hollywood jargon, the Central Plot’s Inciting Incident is the “big hook.” It must occur onscreen because this is the event that incites and captures the audience’s curiosity. Hunger for the answer to the Major Dramatic Question grips the audience’s interest, holding it to the last act’s climax.

用好莱坞术语来说，中心情节的诱发事件就是“关键钩子”。它必须出现在银幕上，因为正是这个事件激发并抓住了观众的好奇心。观众渴望知道这个主要戏剧问题的答案，这种渴望紧紧抓住观众的注意力，直到最后一幕的高潮。

Second, witnessing the Inciting Incident projects an image of the Obligatory Scene into the audience’s imagination. The Obligatory Scene (AKA Crisis) is an event the audience knows it must see before the story can end. This scene will bring the protagonist into a confrontation with the most powerful forces of antagonism in his quest, forces stirred to life by the Inciting Incident that will gather focus and strength through the course of the story. The scene is called “obligatory” because having teased the audience into anticipating this moment, the writer is obligated to keep his promise and show it to them.

其次，目睹了引发事件会在观众的想象中投射出必看场景的画面。必看场景（又称危机）是观众知道在故事结束前必须看到的事件。这一场景将使主人公与他征途中最强大的反派势力正面交锋，这些势力因引发事件而被激发，并在故事发展过程中不断积蓄力量。之所以称之为“必看”，是因为作者既然已经吊足了观众的胃口，让他们期待这一刻的到来，那么他就有义务信守承诺，将其呈现给观众。

JAWS: When the shark attacks a vacationer and the sheriff discovers her remains, an vivid image comes to mind: The shark and the sheriff do battle face-to-face. We don’t know how we’ll get there, or how it’ll turn out. But we do know the film can’t be over until the shark has the sheriff virtually in its jaws. Screenwriter Peter Benchley could not have played this critical event from the point of view of townspeople peering out to sea with binoculars, wondering: “Is that the sheriff? Is that the shark?” BOOM! Then have sheriff and marine biologist (Richard Dreyfuss) swim ashore, shouting, “Oh, what a fight. Let us tell you about it.” Having projected the image in our mind, Benchley was obligated to put us with the sheriff when it happens.

《大白鲨》：当鲨鱼袭击一名度假者，警长发现她的遗体时，一个生动的画面浮现在脑海中：鲨鱼和警长正面搏斗。我们不知道这一幕是如何发生的，也不知道结局如何。但我们知道，只有当鲨鱼几乎将警长咬在嘴里时，电影才能结束。编剧彼得·本奇利不可能仅仅从镇民用望远镜眺望大海、疑惑地问道“那是警长吗？那是鲨鱼吗？”的角度来展现这一关键事件。然后，他让警长和海洋生物学家（理查德·德莱弗斯饰）游到岸边，大喊：“哦，多么精彩的战斗！让我们来告诉你！”既然本奇利已经将这一画面投射到我们的脑海中，他就有义务让我们与警长一同经历这一幕。

Unlike action genres that bring the Obligatory Scene immediately and vividly to mind, other more interior genres hint at this scene in the Inciting Incident, then like a photo negative in acid solution, slowly bring it into focus. In TENDER MERCIES Mac Sledge is drowning in booze and an utterly meaningless life. His ascent from rock bottom begins when he meets a lonely woman with a son who needs a father. He’s inspired to write some new songs, then accepts baptism and tries to make peace with his estranged daughter. Gradually he pieces together a meaningful life.

与动作片那种会立刻让人联想到“必看场景”的类型不同，其他更注重内心描写的类型片会在“诱发事件”中暗示这一场景，然后像酸液中的底片一样，慢慢地将其清晰地呈现出来。在《温柔的怜悯》中，麦克·斯莱奇沉溺于酒精和毫无意义的人生。他从人生低谷中走出来，是因为他遇到了一位孤独的母亲和她渴望父爱的儿子。他受到启发创作了一些新歌，接受了洗礼，并试图与疏远的女儿和解。渐渐地，他开始拼凑出有意义的人生。

The audience, however, senses that because the dragon of meaninglessness drove Sledge to rock bottom, it must once again rear its gruesome head, that the story can’t end until he is slapped in the face with the cruel absurdity of life—this time in all its soul-destroying force. The Obligatory Scene comes in the form of a hideous accident that kills his only child. If a drunk needed an excuse to pick up a bottle again, this would do. Indeed, his daughter’s death plunges his ex-wife into a drugged stupor, but Sledge finds strength to go on.

然而，观众却能感受到，正是因为虚无的恶龙将斯莱奇逼到了人生的谷底，它才必然会再次露出狰狞的面目；故事只有在他被残酷的人生荒诞狠狠地扇了一巴掌——这一次，是它摧毁灵魂的强大力量——之后才会结束。这场必不可少的戏份以一场可怕的意外告终，夺走了他唯一的孩子的生命。如果一个酒鬼需要一个再次拿起酒瓶的借口，这无疑是个绝佳的。的确，女儿的死让他的前妻陷入了药物麻痹的昏沉状态，但斯莱奇却从中找到了继续生活下去的力量。

The death of Sledge’s daughter was “obligatory” in this sense: Suppose Horton Foote had written this scenario: The friendless alcoholic Sledge wakes up one morning with nothing to live for. He meets a woman, falls in love, likes her kid and wants to raise him, finds religion, and writes a new tune. FADE OUT. This isn’t story; it’s daydream. If the quest for meaning has brought about a profound inner change in Sledge, how is Foote to express this? Not through declarations of a change of heart. Self-explanatory dialogue convinces no one. It must be tested by an ultimate event, by pressure-filled character choice and action—the Obligatory (Crisis) Scene and Climax of the last act.

从这个意义上说，斯莱奇女儿的死是“必然的”：假设霍顿·福特写了这样一个场景：孤僻的酒鬼斯莱奇某天早上醒来，感到人生毫无意义。他遇到一个女人，坠入爱河，喜欢她的孩子并想抚养他，皈依宗教，并创作了一首新歌。淡出。这不是故事，而是白日梦。如果对意义的追寻给斯莱奇带来了深刻的内心转变，福特该如何表达呢？不能通过坦诚的内心转变宣言。不言自明的对话无法说服任何人。它必须经受最终事件的考验，经受充满压力的角色选择和行动的考验——即最后一幕的必然（危机）场景和高潮。

When I say that the audience “knows” an Obligatory Scene awaits, it doesn’t know in an objective, checklist sense. If this event is mishandled, the audience won’t exit thinking, “Lousy flick. No Obligatory Scene.” Rather, the audience knows intuitively when something is missing. A lifetime of story ritual has taught the audience to anticipate that the forces of antagonism provoked at the Inciting Incident will build to the limit of human experience, and that the telling cannot end until the protagonist is in some sense face to face with these forces at their most powerful. Linking a story’s Inciting Incident to its Crisis is an aspect of Foreshadowing , the arrangement of early events to prepare for later events. In fact, every choice you make—genre, setting, character, mood—foreshadows. With each line of dialogue or image of action you guide the audience to anticipate certain possibilities, so that when events arrive, they somehow satisfy the expectations you’ve created. The primary component of foreshadowing, however, is the projection of the Obligatory Scene (Crisis) into the audience’s imaginaton by the Inciting Incident.

当我说观众“知道”接下来会有一场“必看场景”时，他们并非客观地、按部就班地去核对。如果这场戏处理不当，观众不会看完后想：“烂片，没有必看场景。”相反，观众凭直觉就能感觉到缺少了什么。长久以来的叙事习惯让观众预感到，在“诱发事件”中激起的对抗力量会不断积聚，直至达到人类经验的极限，而故事只有在主人公以某种方式直面这些力量的巅峰时才能结束。将故事的“诱发事件”与危机联系起来，是伏笔（或伏笔）的一个方面，即通过安排早期事件来为后续事件铺垫。事实上，你做的每一个选择——类型、背景、角色、氛围——都带有伏笔的意味。每一句台词、每一个动作画面，你都在引导观众去预想某些可能性，这样，当事件真正发生时，它们才能以某种方式满足你所创造的预期。然而，伏笔的主要组成部分是通过引发事件将必然场景（危机）投射到观众的想象中。

LOCATING THE INCITING INCIDENT

确定诱发事件

Where to place the Inciting Incident in the overall story design? As a rule of thumb, the first major event of the Central Plot occurs within the first 25 percent of the telling. This is a useful guide, no matter what the medium. How long would you make a theatre audience sit in the dark before engaging the story in a play? Would you make a reader plow through the first hundred pages of a four-hundred-page novel before finding the Central Plot? How long before irredeemable boredom sets in? The standard for a two-hour feature film is to locate the Central Plot’s Inciting Incident somewhere within the first half-hour.

在整体故事结构中，如何安排“导火索”？一般来说，中心情节的第一个重大事件应该发生在故事的前25%之内。无论采用何种媒介，这都是一个有用的指导原则。试想一下，在戏剧中，你会让观众在黑暗中坐多久才开始投入到剧情中？你会让读者在一本四百页的小说中苦读前一百页才找到中心情节吗？多久之后，读者才会感到彻底的厌倦？对于一部两小时的电影来说，通常的做法是将中心情节的导火索安排在前30分钟之内。

It could be the very first thing that happens. In the first thirty seconds of SULLIVAN’S TRAVELS Sullivan (Joel McCrea), a director of vapid but profitable films, defies studio bosses and sets out to make a film with social significance. Within the first two minutes of ON THE WATERFRONT Terry (Marlon Brando) unwittingly helps gangsters murder a friend.

这或许是影片开篇发生的第一件事。《苏利文的旅行》开场仅三十秒，导演苏利文（乔尔·麦克雷饰）——一位擅长拍摄肤浅但盈利的电影的导演——便违抗制片厂老板的命令，决心拍摄一部具有社会意义的影片。《码头风云》开场不到两分钟，特里（马龙·白兰度饰）便在不知情的情况下帮助黑帮谋杀了一位朋友。

Or much later. Twenty-seven minutes into TAXI DRIVER a teenage prostitute, Iris (Jodie Foster), jumps into Travis Bickle’s (Robert De Niro) taxi. Her abusive pimp, Matthew (Harvey Keitel) yanks her back to the street, igniting Travis’s desire to rescue her. A half-hour into ROCKY an obscure club fighter. Rocky Balboa (Sylvester Stallone), agrees to fight Apollo Creed (Carl Weathers) for the heavyweight championship of the world. When Sam plays “As Time Goes By” thirty-two minutes into CASABLANCA, Ilsa suddenly reappears in Rick’s life, launching one of the screen’s great love stories.

或者更晚一些。《出租车司机》开场27分钟，十几岁的妓女艾瑞斯（朱迪·福斯特饰）跳上了特拉维斯·比克尔（罗伯特·德尼罗饰）的出租车。她那虐待成性的皮条客马修（哈维·凯特尔饰）把她拽回了街上，这激起了特拉维斯想要救她的决心。《洛奇》开场半小时，一位名不见经传的拳击手洛奇·巴尔博亚（西尔维斯特·史泰龙饰）同意与阿波罗·克里德（卡尔·韦瑟斯饰）争夺世界重量级拳王头衔。《卡萨布兰卡》开场32分钟，当山姆播放《时光流逝》时，伊尔莎突然出现在里克的生活中，开启了一段银幕上最伟大的爱情故事之一。

Or anywhere in between. However, if the Central Plot’s Inciting Incident arrives much later than fifteen minutes into the film, boredom becomes a risk. Therefore, while the audience waits for the main plot, a subplot may be needed to engage their interest.

或者介于两者之间的任何时间。然而，如果中心情节的触发事件在影片开始超过十五分钟后才出现，观众就有可能感到无聊。因此，在观众等待主线剧情展开期间，可能需要一条副线剧情来吸引他们的兴趣。

In TAXI DRIVER, the subplot of Travis’s lunatic attempt at political assassination grips us. In ROCKY we’re held by the ghetto love story of the painfully shy Adrian (Talia Shire) and the equally troubled Rocky. In CHINATOWN Gittes is duped into investigating Hollis Mulwray for adultery, and this subplot fascinates us as he struggles to untangle himself from the ruse. CASABLANCA’s Act One hooks us with the Inciting Incidents of no fewer than five well-paced subplots.

在《出租车司机》中，特拉维斯疯狂的政治刺杀企图这条支线剧情扣人心弦。在《洛奇》中，我们被贫民窟里害羞内向的艾德里安（塔莉娅·夏尔饰）和同样饱受折磨的洛奇的爱情故事深深吸引。在《唐人街》中，吉特斯被骗去调查霍利斯·穆尔雷的通奸案，他努力摆脱骗局的支线剧情引人入胜。《卡萨布兰卡》第一幕就以五个节奏紧凑的支线剧情的开端牢牢抓住了观众的心。

But why make an audience sit through a subplot, waiting half an hour for the main plot to begin? ROCKY, for example, is in the Sports Genre. Why not start with two quick scenes: The heavyweight champion gives an obscure club fighter a shot at the title (setup), followed by Rocky choosing to take the fight (payoff). Why not open the film with its Central Plot?

但为什么要让观众看完一段支线剧情，等上半个小时才看到主线剧情呢？比如，《洛奇》是体育题材电影。为什么不直接用两个简短的场景开场：重量级拳王给一个名不见经传的俱乐部拳手一次挑战冠军的机会（铺垫），然后洛奇接受挑战（高潮）。为什么不直接以中心剧情开场呢？

Because if ROCKY’s Inciting Incident were the first event we saw, our reaction would have been a shrug and “So what?” Therefore, Stallone uses the first half-hour to delineate Rocky’s world and character with craft and economy, so that when Rocky agrees to the fight, the audience’s reaction is strong and complete: “Him? That loser?!” They sit in shock, dreading the blood-soaked, bone-crushing defeat that lies ahead.

如果洛奇的“导火索”事件是我们看到的第一个场景，我们的反应很可能只是耸耸肩，然后说“那又怎样？”。因此，史泰龙用影片的前半小时，以精湛的技艺和简洁的叙事手法，细致地刻画了洛奇的世界和性格，这样当洛奇同意接受挑战时，观众的反应才会如此强烈而完整：“他？那个失败者？！”他们震惊地坐在那里，恐惧着即将到来的血腥惨败。

Bring in the Central Plot’s Inciting Incident as soon as possible… but not until the moment is ripe.

尽快引入中心情节的导火索事件……但要等到时机成熟。

An Inciting Incident must “hook” the audience, a deep and complete response. Their response must not only be emotional, but rational. This event must not only pull at audience’s feelings, but cause them to ask the Major Dramatic Question and imagine the Obligatory Scene. Therefore, the location of the Central Plot’s Inciting Incident is found in the answer to this question: How much does the audience need to know about the protagonist and his world to have a full response?

一个引爆事件必须“抓住”观众的心，引发他们深刻而完整的反应。这种反应不仅要感性，还要理性。这个事件不仅要触动观众的情感，还要促使他们提出核心戏剧问题，并想象出必然发生的场景。因此，中心情节的引爆事件的位置取决于以下问题的答案：观众需要对主人公及其所处的世界了解多少，才能产生完整的反应？

In some stories, nothing. If an Inciting Incident is archetypal in nature, it requires no setup and must occur immediately. The first sentence of Kafka’s Metamorphosis reads: “One day Gregor Samsa awoke to discover he had been changed into a large cockroach.” KRAMER VS. KRAMER: A wife walks out on her husband and leaves her child with him in the film’s first two minutes. It needs no preparation, for we immediately understand the terrible impact that would have on anybody’s life. JAWS: Shark eats swimmer, sheriff discovers body. These two scenes strike within the first seconds as we instantly grasp the horror.

有些故事里，什么都没有。如果一个引发事件具有原型性质，它就不需要任何铺垫，必须立即发生。卡夫卡的《变形记》第一句话是：“有一天，格里高尔·萨姆沙醒来发现自己变成了一只大蟑螂。”《克莱默夫妇》：影片开头两分钟，妻子就离开了丈夫，把孩子留给了他。这不需要任何铺垫，因为我们立刻就能明白这会对任何人的生活造成多么可怕的影响。《大白鲨》：鲨鱼吞食了游泳者，警长发现了尸体。这两个场景在影片开头几秒钟就震撼人心，我们立刻感受到了恐怖。

Suppose Peter Benchley had opened JAWS with scenes of the sheriff quitting his job with the New York City police and moving out to Amity Island, looking forward to a peaceful life as a law officer in this resort town. We meet his family. We meet the town council and mayor. Early summer brings the tourists. Happy times. Then a shark eats somebody. And suppose Spielberg had been foolish enough to shoot all of this exposition, would we have seen it? No. Editor Verna Fields would have dumped it on the cutting room floor, explaining that all the audience needs to know about the sheriff, his family, the mayor, city council, and tourists will be nicely dramatized in the town’s reaction to the attack… but JAWS starts with the shark.

假设彼得·本奇利在《大白鲨》的开头，展现的是警长辞去纽约市警察局的工作，搬到阿米蒂岛，期待在这个度假小镇过上平静的执法生活。我们认识了他的家人，认识了镇议会和市长。初夏时节，游客纷至沓来。一切都很美好。然后，一条鲨鱼吞噬了某人。假设斯皮尔伯格愚蠢到把所有这些铺垫都拍了下来，我们会看到吗？不会。剪辑师维娜·菲尔兹会把它们统统剪掉，解释说，观众需要了解的关于警长、他的家人、市长、镇议会和游客的一切，都会在小镇对袭击的反应中得到很好的展现……但《大白鲨》的开场就是鲨鱼。

As soon as possible, but not until the moment is ripe… Every story world and cast are different, therefore, every Inciting Incident is a different event located at a different point. If it arrives too soon, the audience may be confused. If it arrives too late, the audience may be bored. The instant the audience has a sufficient understanding of character and world to react fully, execute your Inciting Incident. Not a scene earlier, or a scene later. The exact moment is found as much by feeling as by analysis.

越早越好，但也要等到时机成熟……每个故事的世界观和角色都不同，因此，每个触发事件都是一个发生在不同时间点的不同事件。如果出现得太早，观众可能会感到困惑；如果出现得太晚，观众可能会感到无聊。只有当观众对角色和世界观有了足够的了解，能够做出完整的反应时，才能触发你的触发事件。不要提前或延后任何一幕。找到这个恰当的时机，既要依靠感觉，也要依靠分析。

If we writers have a common fault in design and placement of the Inciting Incident, it’s that we habitually delay the Central Plot while we pack our opening sequences with exposition. We consistently underestimate knowledge and life experience of the audience, laying out our characters and world with tedious details the filmgoer has already filled in with common sense.

如果我们编剧在设计和安排冲突事件方面存在一个共同的缺陷，那就是我们习惯性地拖延中心情节的展开，而将大量的背景介绍塞进开场。我们总是低估观众的知识水平和生活经验，用冗长乏味的细节来描绘人物和世界，而这些细节观众早已凭借常识自行脑补。

Ingmar Bergman is one of the cinema’s best directors because he is, in my opinion, the cinema’s finest screenwriter. And the one quality that stands above all the others in Bergman’s writing is his extreme economy—how little he tells us about anything. In his THROUGH A GLASS DARKLY, for example, all we ever learn about his four characters is that the father is a widowed, best-selling novelist, his son-in-law a doctor, his son a student, and his daughter a schizophrenic, suffering from the same illness that killed her mother. She’s been released from a mental hospital to join her family for a few days by the sea, and that act alone upsets the balance of forces in all their lives, propelling a powerful drama from the first moments.

在我看来，英格玛·伯格曼是影史上最伟大的导演之一，因为他也是影史上最杰出的编剧。伯格曼的剧本最突出的特点就是他极简的叙事风格——他几乎不透露任何信息。例如，在他的《透过黑暗的玻璃》中，我们对四个主要人物的了解仅限于：父亲是一位畅销小说家，已丧偶；女婿是一位医生；儿子是一位学生；女儿患有精神分裂症，与她的母亲一样，都死于这种疾病。她从精神病院出院，与家人在海边共度几天时光，而仅仅是这一举动就打破了他们所有人生活的平衡，从一开始就推动着剧情的发展，扣人心弦。

No book-signing scenes to help us understand that the father is a commercial but not critical success. No scenes in an operating room to demonstrate the doctor’s profession. No boarding school scenes to explain how much the son needs his father. No electric shock treatment sessions to explain the daughter’s anguish. Bergman knows that his urbane audience quickly grasps the implications behind best-seller, doctor, boarding school, and mental hospital… and that less is always more.

没有签售会的场景来帮助我们理解这位父亲畅销却不被评论界认可。没有手术室的场景来展现医生的职业。没有寄宿学校的场景来解释儿子有多么需要父亲。没有电击治疗的场景来解释女儿的痛苦。伯格曼深知，他那些见多识广的观众很快就能领会畅销书、医生、寄宿学校和精神病院背后的含义……而且，少即是多。

THE QUALITY OF THE INCITING INCIDENT

诱发事件的性质

A favorite joke among film distributors goes like this: A typical European film opens with golden, sunlit clouds. Cut to even more splendid, bouffant clouds. Cut again to yet more magnificent, rubescent clouds. A Hollywood film opens with golden, billowing clouds. In the second shot a 747 jumbo jet comes out of the clouds. In the third, it explodes.

电影发行商之间有个很流行的笑话：一部典型的欧洲电影以金色的阳光照耀下的云朵开场。镜头切换到更加壮丽蓬松的云朵。再切一刀，又是一片绚丽的红云。好莱坞电影的开头是金色的翻滚云朵。第二个镜头，一架747巨型喷气式客机从云层中飞出。第三个镜头，它爆炸了。

What quality of event need an Inciting Incident be?

引发事件需要具备怎样的性质？

ORDINARY PEOPLE carries a Central Plot and subplot that are often mistaken for each other because of their unconventional design. Conrad (Timothy Hutton) is the protagonist of the film’s subplot with an Inciting Incident that takes the life of his older brother during a storm at sea. Conrad survives but is guilt-ridden and suicidal. The brother’s death is in the Backstory and is dramatized in flashback at the Crisis/Climax of the subplot when Conrad relives the boating accident and chooses to live.

《普通人》的主线剧情和副线剧情常常因为其非传统的叙事结构而被混淆。康拉德（蒂莫西·赫顿饰）是副线剧情的主角，他的哥哥在海上风暴中丧生，这起事件成为了他故事的导火索。康拉德虽然幸存下来，却饱受内疚折磨，甚至一度想要自杀。哥哥的死被放在了背景故事中，并在副线剧情的高潮/危机时刻以倒叙的方式呈现：康拉德重温了那场海难，并最终选择了活下去。

The Central Plot is driven by Conrad’s father, Calvin (Donald Sutherland). Although seemingly passive, he is by definition the protagonist: the empathetic character with the will and capacity to pursue desire to the end of the line. Throughout the film, Calvin is on a quest for the cruel secret that haunts his family and makes reconciliation between his son and wife impossible. After a painful struggle, he finds it: His wife hates Conrad, not since the death of her older son, but since Conrad’s birth.

影片的核心情节由康拉德的父亲卡尔文（唐纳德·萨瑟兰饰）推动。尽管他看似被动，但从本质上讲，他才是主角：一个富有同情心、意志坚定且有能力将欲望追寻到底的角色。整部影片中，卡尔文都在追寻一个残酷的秘密，这个秘密一直困扰着他的家庭，也使得他的儿子和妻子无法和解。经过一番痛苦的挣扎，他终于找到了答案：他的妻子恨康拉德，并非因为长子的去世，而是从康拉德出生起就恨他。

At the Crisis Calvin confronts his wife, Beth (Mary Tyler Moore) with the truth: She’s an obsessively orderly woman who wanted only one child. When her second son came along, she resented his craving for love when she could love only her first-born. She’s always hated Conrad, and he’s always felt it. This is why he’s been suicidal over his brother’s death. Calvin then forces the Climax: She must learn to love Conrad or leave. Beth goes to a closet, packs a suitcase, and heads out the door. She cannot face her inability to love her son.

在危机时刻，卡尔文（Calvin）向妻子贝丝（Beth，玛丽·泰勒·摩尔饰）坦白：她是个有强迫症的守规矩的女人，只想要一个孩子。当第二个儿子出生后，她无法接受他对爱的渴望，因为她只能爱自己的长子。她一直憎恨康拉德（Conrad），而康拉德也一直感受到了这一点。这就是他因哥哥的死而想要自杀的原因。卡尔文随后逼迫她接受现实：她必须学会爱康拉德，否则就离开。贝丝走进衣橱，收拾好行李箱，走出了家门。她无法面对自己无法爱儿子的事实。

This Climax answers the Major Dramatic Question: Will the family solve its problems within itself or be torn apart? Working backward from it, we seek the Inciting Incident, the event that has upset the balance of Calvin’s life and sent him on his quest.

这一高潮解答了主要的戏剧性问题：这个家庭能否自行解决问题，还是会分崩离析？从这里倒推，我们寻找引发事件，也就是打破卡尔文生活平衡并促使他踏上寻觅之旅的事件。

The film opens with Conrad coming home from a psychiatric hospital, presumably cured of his suicidal neurosis. Calvin feels that the family has survived its loss and balance has been restored. The next morning Conrad, in a grim mood, sits opposite his father at the breakfast table. Beth puts a plate of French toast under her son’s face. He refuses to eat. She snatches the plate away, marches to the sink, and scrapes his breakfast down a garbage disposal, muttering: “You can’t keep French toast.”

影片开头，康拉德从精神病院回家，想必已经治愈了自杀倾向。卡尔文觉得家里已经走出了失去亲人的阴影，生活恢复了平衡。第二天早上，康拉德心情低落，坐在餐桌对面，和父亲一起吃早餐。贝丝把一盘法式吐司放在儿子面前。他一口也不肯吃。贝丝一把抢过盘子，走到水槽边，把儿子的早餐刮进垃圾处理器，一边嘟囔着：“你不能吃法式吐司。”

Director Robert Redford’s camera cuts to the father as the man’s life crashes. Calvin instantly senses that the hatred is back with a vengeance. Behind it hides something fearful. This chilling event grips the audience with dread as it reacts, thinking: “Look what she did to her child! He’s just home from the hospital and she’s doing this number on him.”

导演罗伯特·雷德福的镜头切换到父亲身上，此时男人的生活彻底崩溃。卡尔文立刻察觉到仇恨卷土重来，而且来势汹汹。仇恨背后隐藏着可怕的东西。这一幕令人不寒而栗，观众不禁感到恐惧，心想：“看看她对自己的孩子做了什么！他刚出院回家，她就这么对他！”

Novelist Judith Guest and screenwriter Alvin Sargent gave Calvin a quiet characterization, a man who won’t leap up from the table and try to bully wife and son into reconciliation. His first thought is to give them time and loving encouragements, such as the family photo scene. When he learns of Conrad’s troubles at school, he hires a psychiatrist for him. He talks gently with his wife, hoping to understand.

小说家朱迪思·盖斯特和编剧阿尔文·萨金特将卡尔文塑造成一个沉稳内敛的人物，他不会像某些人那样突然从餐桌旁跳起来，试图强迫妻子和儿子和解。他首先想到的是给予他们时间和充满爱意的鼓励，比如拍摄全家福的那一幕。当他得知康拉德在学校遇到困难时，他为儿子请了一位心理医生。他温和地与妻子交谈，希望能理解她的处境。

Because Calvin is a hesitant, compassionate man, Sargent had to build the dynamic of the film’s progressions around the subplot. Conrad’s struggle with suicide is far more active than Calvin’s subtle quest. So Sargent foregrounded the boy’s subplot, giving it inordinate emphasis and screentime, while carefully increasing the momentum of the Central Plot in the background. By the time the subplot ends in the psychiatrist’s office, Calvin is ready to bring the Central Plot to its devastating end. The point, however, is that the Inciting Incident of ORDINARY PEOPLE is triggered by a woman scraping French toast down a garbage disposal.

由于卡尔文是一个犹豫不决却又富有同情心的人，萨金特不得不围绕着这条副线来构建影片的叙事节奏。康拉德与自杀的斗争远比卡尔文的隐晦探索更加直接有力。因此，萨金特将男孩的副线置于聚光灯下，给予其大量的篇幅和强调，同时巧妙地在背景中推进主线剧情的发展。当副线在精神科医生的办公室结束时，卡尔文已经准备好将主线剧情推向令人心碎的结局。然而，关键在于，《普通人》的导火索竟然是一位女士将法式吐司刮入垃圾处理器的场景。

Henry James wrote brilliantly about story art in the prefaces to his novels, and once asked: “What, after all, is an event?” An event, he said, could be as little as a woman putting her hand on the table and looking at you “that certain way.” In the right context, just a gesture and a look could mean, “I’ll never see you again,” or “I’ll love you forever”—a life broken or made.

亨利·詹姆斯在其小说序言中对故事艺术进行了精彩的论述，他曾问道：“究竟什么是事件？”他认为，事件可以小到一位女士将手放在桌上，用“那种眼神”看着你。在恰当的语境下，一个手势和一个眼神就可能意味着“我再也见不到你了”，或者“我会永远爱你”——一段人生就此破碎或成就。

The quality of the Inciting Incident (for that matter, any event) must be germane to the world, characters, and genre surrounding it. Once it is conceived, the writer must concentrate on its function. Does the Inciting Incident radically upset the balance of forces in the protagonist’s life? Does it arouse in the protagonist the desire to restore balance? Does it inspire in him the conscious desire for that object, material or immaterial, he feels would restore the balance? In a complex protagonist, does it also bring to life an unconscious desire that contradicts his conscious need? Does it launch the protagonist on a quest for his desire? Does it raise the Major Dramatic Question in the mind of the audience? Does it project an image of the Obligatory Scene? If it does all this, then it can be as little as a woman putting her hand on the table, looking at you “that certain way.”

引发事件（或者说任何事件）的质量必须与它所处的世界、人物和类型相契合。一旦构思完成，作者就必须专注于它的功能。引发事件是否从根本上打破了主人公生活中的力量平衡？它是否唤起了主人公恢复平衡的渴望？它是否激发了主人公对某种他认为能够恢复平衡的物质或非物质对象的有意识的渴望？对于一个复杂的主人公而言，它是否也揭示了一种与他有意识的需求相矛盾的潜意识欲望？它是否开启了主人公追寻欲望的旅程？它是否在观众心中提出了主要的戏剧性问题？它是否展现了必要的场景？如果它做到了所有这些，那么它甚至可以是一个女人把手放在桌子上，用“那种眼神”看着你这样简单的举动。

CREATING THE INCITING INCIDENT

引发事件的产生

The Climax of the last act is far and away the most difficult scene to create: It’s the soul of the telling. If it doesn’t work, the story doesn’t work. But the second most difficult scene to write is the Central Plot’s Inciting Incident. We rewrite this scene more than any other. So here are some questions to ask that should help bring it to mind.

最后一幕的高潮无疑是最难创作的场景：它是故事的灵魂。如果高潮部分失败了，整个故事也就失败了。但第二难写的场景是中心情节的触发事件。我们修改这个场景的次数比其他任何场景都多。所以，以下几个问题或许能帮助你更好地构思这个场景。

What is the worst possible thing that could happen to my protagonist? How could that turn out to be the best possible thing that could happen to him?

我的主人公可能遇到的最糟糕的事情是什么？而这件事又怎么可能最终变成他遇到的最好的事情呢？

KRAMER VS. KRAMER. The worst: Disaster strikes the workaholic Kramer (Dustin Hoffman) when his wife walks out on him and her child. The best: This turns out to be the shock he needed to fulfill his unconscious desire to be a loving human being.

《克莱默夫妇》。最糟糕的是：工作狂克莱默（达斯汀·霍夫曼饰）遭遇了人生的重大打击——妻子带着孩子离开了他。最好的是：这反而成了他内心深处渴望成为一个充满爱心的人的契机。

AN UNMARRIED WOMAN. The worst: When her husband says he’s leaving her for another woman, Erica (Jill Clayburgh) retches. The best: His exit turns out to be the freeing experience that allows this male-dependent woman to fulfill her unconscious desire for independence and self-possession.

一位未婚女性。最糟糕的是：当丈夫说要离开她去和另一个女人在一起时，艾丽卡（吉尔·克莱伯格饰）感到一阵恶心。最好的是：丈夫的离开反而成了她获得解脱的契机，让她这个依赖男性的女性得以实现内心深处对独立和自主的渴望。

Or: What’s the best possible thing that could happen to my protagonist? How could it become the worst possible thing?

或者：对我主人公来说，最好的事情是什么？它又如何会变成最糟糕的事情？

DEATH IN VENICE. Von Aschenbach (Dirk Bogarde) has lost his wife and children to a plague. Since then he’s buried himself in his work to the point of physical and mental collapse. His doctor sends him to the Venice spa to recuperate. The best: There he falls madly, helplessly in love… but with a boy. His passion for the impossibly beautiful youth, and the impossibility of it, leads to despair. The worst: When a new plague invades Venice and the child’s mother hurries her son away, Von Aschenbach lingers to wait for death and escape from his misery.

威尼斯之死。冯·阿申巴赫（德克·博加德饰）的妻子和孩子死于瘟疫。此后，他埋头工作，直至身心崩溃。医生建议他前往威尼斯疗养。最精彩的是：在那里，他疯狂地、无可救药地爱上了一个男孩。他对这个俊美绝伦的少年的痴迷，以及这段感情的遥不可及，最终将他推向绝望。更糟糕的是：当新的瘟疫席卷威尼斯，男孩的母亲匆忙带着儿子离开时，冯·阿申巴赫却留了下来，等待死亡的降临，以求摆脱这无尽的痛苦。

THE GODFATHER, PART II. The best: After Michael (Al Pacino) is made Don of the Corleone crime family, he decides to take his family into the legitimate world. The worst: His ruthless enforcement of the mafia code of loyalty ends in the assassination of his closest associates, estrangement from his wife and children, and the murder of his brother, leaving him a hollowed-out, desolate man.

《教父2》。精彩之处：迈克尔（阿尔·帕西诺饰）成为科里昂家族的教父后，决定带领家族走向合法世界。不足之处：他对黑手党忠诚准则的残酷执行，最终导致他最亲密的同伙被暗杀，与妻子儿女疏远，甚至连自己的兄弟也被杀害，使他变成了一个内心空洞、孤独寂寞的人。

A story may turn more than one cycle of this pattern. What is the best? How could that become the worst? How could that reverse yet again into the protagonist’s salvation? Or: What is the worst? How could that become the best? How could that lead the protagonist to damnation? We stretch toward the “bests” and “worsts” because story—when it is art—is not about the middle ground of human experience.

一个故事可能会经历不止一次这样的循环。什么是最好的？它怎么会变成最坏的？它又怎么会再次逆转，成为主人公的救赎？或者：什么是最坏的？它怎么会变成最好的？它又怎么会将主人公引向毁灭？我们追求“最好”与“最坏”，因为故事——当它成为艺术时——并非关乎人类经验的中间地带。

The impact of the Inciting Incident creates our opportunity to reach the limits of life. It’s a kind of explosion. In Action genres it may be in fact an explosion: in other films, as muted as a smile. No matter how subtle or direct, it must upset the status quo of the protagonist and jolt his life from its existing pattern, so that chaos invades the character’s universe. Out of this upheaval, you must find, at Climax, a resolution, for better or worse, that rearranges this universe into a new order.

诱发事件的影响创造了我们触及生命极限的机会。它是一种爆发。在动作片中，它可能确实是一场爆炸；而在其他类型的电影中，它可能像一个微笑一样悄无声息。无论它多么微妙或直接，它都必须打破主人公的现状，使其生活脱离原有的模式，从而让混乱侵入角色的世界。在这场剧变中，你必须在高潮处找到一个解决方案，无论好坏，这个方案都将重塑这个世界，使其恢复到新的秩序。

#↩

9
9
ACT DESIGN
ACT 设计

PROGRESSIVE COMPLICATIONS

进行性并发症

The second element of the five-part design is Progressive Complications: that great sweeping body of story that spans from Inciting Incident to Crisis/Climax of the final act. To complicate means to make life difficult for characters. To complicate progressively means to generate more and more conflict as they face greater and greater forces of antagonism, creating a succession of events that passes points of no return.

五段式叙事结构的第二个要素是渐进式复杂化：它指的是从导火事件到最终高潮/危机的宏大叙事结构。复杂化意味着让角色们的生活更加艰难。渐进式复杂化则意味着随着他们面对越来越强大的敌对势力，冲突也越来越多，从而引发一系列无法挽回的事件。

Points of No Return

不归路

The Inciting Incident launches the protagonist on a quest for a conscious or unconscious Object of Desire to restore life’s balance. To begin the pursuit of his desire, he takes a minimum, conservative action to provoke a positive response from his reality. But the effect of his action is to arouse forces of antagonism from inner, personal, or social/environmental Levels of Conflict that block his desire, cracking open the Gap between expectation and result.

诱发事件促使主人公踏上寻找有意识或无意识的欲望对象的旅程，以期恢复生活的平衡。为了开始追求欲望，他采取了一种最低限度的、保守的行动，试图从现实中获得积极的回应。然而，他的行动却激起了来自内在、个人或社会/环境层面的对抗力量，这些力量阻碍了他的欲望，最终导致预期与结果之间的差距扩大。

When the Gap opens, the audience realizes that this is a point of no return. Minimal efforts won’t work. The character can’t restore the balance of life by taking lesser actions. Henceforth, all action like the character’s first effort, actions of minor quality and magnitude, must be eliminated from the story.

当裂痕出现时，观众意识到这是一个无法挽回的转折点。任何微不足道的努力都无济于事。角色无法通过采取次要的行动来恢复生活的平衡。因此，所有像角色最初尝试那样，质量和影响都微不足道的行动，都必须从故事中剔除。

Realizing he’s at risk, the protagonist draws upon greater willpower and capacity to struggle through this gap and take a second, more difficult action. But again the effect is to provoke forces of antagonism, opening a second gap between expectation and result.

意识到自己身处险境，主人公鼓起更强大的意志力和能力，努力克服眼前的困难，采取了第二个更为艰难的行动。然而，此举却再次激起了敌对势力，在预期与结果之间造成了第二次差距。

The audience now senses that this too is a point of no return. Moderate actions like the second won’t succeed. Therefore, all actions of this magnitude and quality must be eliminated.

观众现在意识到，这也是一个无法挽回的局面。像第二种情况那样的温和措施不会奏效。因此，所有此类规模和性质的行动都必须被禁止。

At greater risk, the character must adjust to his changed circumstances and take an action that demands even more willpower and personal capacity, expecting or at least hoping for a helpful or manageable reaction from his world. But once more the gap flies open as even more powerful forces of antagonism react to his third action.

面临更大的风险，角色必须适应变化的环境，采取一项需要更强意志力和个人能力的行动，并期待或至少希望得到外界的积极或可控的回应。然而，随着更加强大的敌对势力对他的第三次行动做出反应，裂痕再次扩大。

Again, the audience recognizes that this is yet another point of no return. The more extreme actions won’t get the character what he wants, so these too are canceled out of consideration.

观众再次意识到，这又是一个无法挽回的局面。更极端的行动并不能让角色达成所愿，因此这些行动也被排除在外。

Progressions build by drawing upon greater and greater capacities from characters, demanding greater and greater willpower from them, putting them at greater and greater risk, constantly passing points of no return in terms of the magnitude or quality of action.

剧情的发展是通过挖掘角色越来越强大的能力，要求他们拥有越来越强大的意志力，让他们面临越来越大的风险，不断地跨越行动的规模或质量上的不归点来实现的。

A story must not retreat to actions of lesser quality or magnitude, but move progressively forward to a final action beyond which the audience cannot imagine another.

故事不应退回到质量或规模较小的情节，而应逐步推进到最终的情节，让观众无法想象还有什么比这更精彩的。

How many times have you had this experience? A film begins well, hooking you into the lives of the characters. It builds with strong interest over the first half-hour to a major Turning Point. But then forty or fifty minutes into the film, it starts to drag. Your eyes wander from the screen; you glance at your watch; you wish you’d bought more popcorn; you start paying attention to the anatomy of the person you came with. Perhaps the film gains pace again and finishes well, but for twenty or thirty flabby minutes in the middle you lost interest.

你经历过多少次这样的情况？一部电影开头很精彩，引人入胜，让你沉浸在角色的生活中。前半小时剧情紧凑，扣人心弦，直至一个重要的转折点。但四五十分钟后，电影开始拖沓。你的目光游离屏幕；你不时瞥一眼手表；你后悔没多买点爆米花；你甚至开始关注同伴的身体构造。或许电影最后又恢复了节奏，结尾也不错，但中间那二三十分钟的冗长乏味让你失去了兴趣。

If you look closely at the soft bellies that hang out over the belt of so many films, you’ll discover that this is where the writer’s insight and imagination went limp. He couldn’t build progressions, so in effect he put the story in retrograde. In the middle of Act Two he’s given his characters lesser actions of the kind they’ve already done in Act One—not identical actions but actions of a similar size or kind: minimal, conservative, and by now trivial. As we watch, our instincts tell us that these actions didn’t get the character what he wanted in Act One, therefore they’re not going to get him what he wants in Act Two. The writer is recycling story and we’re treading water.

如果你仔细观察许多电影中那些松垮垮的情节，你会发现，这正是编剧洞察力和想象力枯竭的地方。他无法构建情节发展，实际上却让故事倒退了。在第二幕中段，他让角色们做了些与第一幕中类似的、无关紧要的事情——并非完全相同，而是规模或性质相似的举动：微不足道、保守，而且如今已显得无关紧要。当我们观看时，我们的直觉告诉我们，这些举动在第一幕中并没有让角色达成所愿，因此在第二幕中也同样行不通。编剧在重复利用故事，而我们却原地踏步。

The only way to keep a film’s current flowing and rising is research—imagination, memory, fact. Generally, a feature-length Archplot is designed around forty to sixty scenes that conspire into twelve to eighteen sequences that build into three or more acts that top one another continuously to the end of the line. To create forty to sixty scenes and not repeat yourself , you need to invent hundreds. After sketching this mountain of material, tunnel to find those few gems that will build sequences and acts into memorable and moving points of no return. For if you devise only the forty to sixty scenes needed to fill the 120 pages of a screenplay, your work is almost certain to be antiprogressive and repetitious.

保持电影情节流畅推进的唯一途径是研究——想象力、记忆和事实。通常，一部长篇电影的宏大叙事结构围绕着四十到六十个场景展开，这些场景交织成十二到十八个段落，最终构成三个或更多幕，层层递进，直至结尾。为了创作出四十到六十个场景而不重复，你需要构思数百个场景。在勾勒出这堆积如山的素材之后，你需要深入挖掘，找到那些能够将段落和幕构建成令人难忘、感人至深的转折点的精华。因为如果你仅仅为了填满120页剧本而构思四十到六十个场景，那么你的作品几乎注定会缺乏创新，并且重复乏味。

The Law of Conflict

冲突法

When the protagonist steps out of the Inciting Incident, he enters a world governed by the Law of Conflict. To wit: Nothing moves forward in a story except through conflict.

当主人公走出“诱发事件”时，他便进入了一个由冲突法则支配的世界。也就是说：故事的发展离不开冲突。

Put another way, conflict is to storytelling what sound is to music. Both story and music are temporal arts, and the single most difficult task of the temporal artist is to hook our interest, hold our uninterrupted concentration, then carry us through time without an awareness of the passage of time.

换句话说，冲突之于故事，正如声音之于音乐。故事和音乐都是时间性的艺术，而时间性艺术家最难的任务就是抓住我们的兴趣，让我们全神贯注，然后带领我们穿越时间，让我们在不知不觉中感受时间的流逝。

In music, this effect is accomplished through sound. Instruments or voices capture us and move us along, making time vanish. Suppose we were listening to a symphony and the orchestra suddenly fell silent. What would be the effect? First, confusion as we wonder why they’ve stopped, then very quickly we would hear in our imaginations the sound of a ticking clock. We would become acutely aware of the passage of time, and because time is so subjective, if the orchestra were silent for just three minutes, it would seem like thirty.

在音乐中，这种效果是通过声音实现的。乐器或人声吸引着我们，引领我们进入音乐的世界，使时间仿佛消失。假设我们正在聆听交响乐，乐团突然停止了演奏。会产生什么效果呢？首先，我们会感到困惑，想知道他们为什么停止了演奏；然后，很快，我们的脑海中就会响起滴答作响的钟声。我们会敏锐地意识到时间的流逝，而由于时间是如此主观，如果乐团仅仅停止演奏了三分钟，我们也会感觉像过了三十分钟。

The music of story is conflict. As long as conflict engages our thoughts and emotions we travel through the hours unaware of the voyage. Then suddenly the film’s over. We glance at our watches, amazed. But when conflict disappears, so do we. The pictorial interest of eye-pleasing photography or the aural pleasures of a beautiful score may hold us briefly, but if conflict is kept on hold for too long, our eyes leave the screen. And when our eyes leave the screen they take thought and emotion with them.

故事的乐章在于冲突。只要冲突牵动着我们的思绪和情感，我们便会在不知不觉中度过数小时。然后，电影突然结束。我们瞥了一眼手表，惊讶不已。但当冲突消失时，我们也随之消散。赏心悦目的摄影画面或优美的配乐或许能短暂地吸引我们，但如果冲突长时间被搁置，我们的目光就会离开屏幕。而当我们的目光离开屏幕时，我们的思绪和情感也随之消逝。

The Law of Conflict is more than an aesthetic principle; it is the soul of story. Story is metaphor for life, and to be alive is to be in seemingly perpetual conflict. As Jean-Paul Sartre expressed it, the essence of reality is scarcity, a universal and eternal lacking. There isn’t enough of anything in this world to go around. Not enough food, not enough love, not enough justice, and never enough time. Time, as Heidegger observed, is the basic category of existence. We live in its ever-shrinking shadow, and if we are to achieve anything in our brief being that lets us die without feeling we’ve wasted our time, we will have to go into heady conflict with the forces of scarcity that deny our desires.

冲突法则不仅仅是一个美学原则，它是故事的灵魂。故事是人生的隐喻，而活着本身就意味着身处看似永恒的冲突之中。正如让-保罗·萨特所言，现实的本质是匮乏，一种普遍而永恒的缺失。这世上没有什么东西是足够分配的。食物不够，爱不够，正义不够，时间也永远不够。正如海德格尔所观察到的，时间是存在的基本范畴。我们生活在它不断缩小的阴影之下，如果我们想要在短暂的生命中有所成就，让我们在离世时不感到虚度光阴，我们就必须与那剥夺我们欲望的匮乏力量展开一场激烈的斗争。

Writers who cannot grasp the truth of our transitory existence, who have been mislead by the counterfeit comforts of the modern world, who believe that life is easy once you know how to play the game, give conflict a false inflection. Their scripts fail for one of two reasons: either a glut of meaningless and absurdly violent conflict, or a vacancy of meaningful and honestly expressed conflict.

那些无法领悟我们生命短暂真谛、被现代社会虚假的安逸所蒙蔽、误以为只要掌握了游戏规则人生就一帆风顺的作家，赋予了冲突一种虚假的意味。他们的剧本失败的原因不外乎以下两点：要么充斥着毫无意义且荒谬暴力的冲突，要么缺乏有意义且真诚表达的冲突。

The former are exercises in turbo special effects, written by those who follow textbook imperatives to create conflict, but, because they’re disinterested in or insensitive to the honest struggles of life, devise phony, overwrought excuses for mayhem.

前者是特效炫技之作，作者遵循教科书式的规则制造冲突，但由于他们对生活中真实的挣扎漠不关心或麻木不仁，所以编造出虚假、夸张的借口来制造混乱。

The latter are tedious portraits written in reaction against conflict itself. These writers take the Pollyanna view that life would really be nice… if it weren’t for conflict. Therefore, their films avoid it in favor of low-key depictions to suggest that if we learned to communicate a little better, be a little more charitable, respect the environment, humanity could return to paradise. But if history has taught us anything, it’s that when toxic nightmare is finally cleaned up, the homeless provided shelter, and the world converted to solar energy, each of us will still be up to our eyebrows in mulch.

后者是些乏味的描绘，是对冲突本身的一种反抗。这些作家抱持着一种盲目乐观的观点：如果没有冲突，生活该有多美好。因此，他们的电影刻意回避冲突，转而采用低调的描绘，暗示如果我们学会更好地沟通、更加仁慈、尊重环境，人类就能重返天堂。但历史告诉我们，即便毒瘤最终被清除，无家可归者得到了庇护，世界也转向了太阳能，我们每个人仍然会深陷泥泞之中。

Writers at these extremes fail to realize that while the quality of conflict changes as it shifts from level to level, the quantity of conflict in life is constant. Something is always lacking. Like squeezing a balloon, the volume of conflict never changes, it just bulges in another direction. When we remove conflict from one level of life, it amplifies ten times over on another level.

这些极端观点的作者未能意识到，尽管冲突的性质会随着层次的变化而改变，但生活中冲突的数量却是恒定的。总有一些东西缺失。就像挤压气球一样，冲突的体积从未改变，它只是向另一个方向膨胀。当我们从生活的一个层次中移除冲突时，它在另一个层次上会放大十倍。

If, for example, we manage to satisfy our external desires and find harmony with the world, in short order serenity turns to boredom. Now Sartre’s “scarcity” is the absence of conflict itself. Boredom is the inner conflict we suffer when we lose desire, when we lack a lacking. What’s worse, if we were to put on screen the conflictless existence of a character who, day-in, day-out, lives in placid contentment, the boredom in the audience would be palpably painful.

例如，如果我们能够满足外在欲望，与世界和谐相处，那么平静很快就会变成无聊。萨特所说的“稀缺”指的是冲突本身的缺失。无聊则是我们失去欲望、缺乏某种缺失时所经历的内在冲突。更糟糕的是，如果我们把一个日复一日生活在平静满足中的人物毫无冲突的生活搬上银幕，观众的无聊感将会是显而易见的。

By and large, the struggle for physical survival has been eliminated for the educated classes of the industrialized nations. This security from the outside world gives us time to reflect on the world inside. Once housed, dressed, fed, and medicated, we take a breath and realize how incomplete we are as human beings. We want more than physical comfort, we want, of all things, happiness, and so begin the wars of the inner life.

总的来说，工业化国家受过教育的阶层已经摆脱了为生存而挣扎的困境。这种来自外部世界的安全感让我们有时间反思内心世界。一旦有了住所、衣物、食物和药物，我们便能喘口气，意识到作为人类，我们是多么的不完整。我们想要的不仅仅是物质上的舒适，我们渴望的，莫过于幸福，于是，内心世界的战争便开始了。

If, as a writer, however, you find that the conflicts of mind, body, emotions, and soul do not interest you, then look into the Third World and see how the rest of humanity lives. The majority suffer short, painful existences, ridden with disease and hunger, terrorized by tyranny and lawless violence, without hope that life will ever be any different for their children.

然而，如果你作为一名作家，对心灵、肉体、情感和灵魂的冲突不感兴趣，那么不妨关注一下第三世界，看看其他人的生活状况。他们中的大多数人过着短暂而痛苦的生活，饱受疾病和饥饿的折磨，生活在暴政和无法无天的暴力阴影下，看不到子孙后代未来生活会有任何改变的希望。

If the depth and breadth of conflict in the inner life and the greater world do not move you, let this: death. Death is like a freight train in the future, heading toward us, closing the hours, second by second, between now and then. If we’re to live with any sense of satisfaction, we must engage life’s forces of antagonism before the train arrives.

如果内心世界和外部世界冲突的深度和广度都无法触动你，那么就让死亡来震撼你吧。死亡就像一列驶向我们未来的货运列车，一秒一秒地缩短着从现在到那时的时间。如果我们想要活得充实而有意义，就必须在列车到来之前，直面人生中的种种对抗力量。

An artist intent on creating works of lasting quality comes to realize that life isn’t about subtle adjustments to stress, or hyper-conflicts of master criminals with stolen nuclear devices holding cities for ransom. Life is about the ultimate questions of finding love and self-worth, of bringing serenity to inner chaos, of the titanic social inequities everywhere around us, of time running out. Life is conflict. That is its nature. The writer must decide where and how to orchestrate this struggle.

一位致力于创作经久不衰作品的艺术家逐渐意识到，生活并非在于微妙地调整以应对压力，也并非在于犯罪头目劫持核武器勒索城市等极端冲突。生活关乎终极问题：寻找爱与自我价值，在内心的混乱中寻求平静，直面我们周围无处不在的巨大社会不公，以及时间的流逝。生活本身就是冲突。这是它的本质。作家必须决定在何处以及如何安排这场斗争。

Complication Versus Complexity

复杂性与复杂性

To complicate a story the writer builds conflict progressively to the end of the line. Difficult enough. But the task increases geometrically when we take story from mere complication to full complexity.

为了让故事更加复杂，作者会逐步构建冲突，直至故事结尾。这本身就够难了。但当我们把故事从简单的复杂化推向完全的复杂性时，难度会呈几何级数增长。

Conflict may come, as we’ve seen, from any one, two, or all three of the levels of antagonism. To simply complicate a story means to place all conflict on only one of these three levels.

正如我们所见，冲突可能源于对抗的任何一个、两个或全部三个层面。简单地将故事复杂化，意味着将所有冲突都集中在这三个层面中的一个。

From the Horror Film to Action/Adventure to Farce , action heroes face conflict only on the extra-personal level. James Bond, for example, has no inner conflicts, nor would we mistake his encounters with women as personal—they’re recreational.

从恐怖片到动作冒险片再到闹剧，动作英雄面临的冲突都仅限于个人层面之外。例如，詹姆斯·邦德没有内心冲突，我们也不会把他与女性的交往误认为是私人恩怨——那只是娱乐消遣。

COMPLICATION:
复杂程度：
CONFLICT AT ONLY ONE LEVEL
仅在一个层面上存在冲突

INNER CONFLICT — Stream of Consciousness

内心冲突——意识流

PERSONAL CONFLICT — Soap Opera

个人冲突——肥皂剧

EXTRA-PERSONAL CONFLICT — Action/Adventure, Farce

超个人冲突——动作/冒险，闹剧

Complicated films share two hallmarks. The first is a large cast. If the writer restricts the protagonist to social conflict, he’ll need, as the advertising declares, “a cast of thousands.” James Bond faces arch-villains along with their minions, assassins, femmes fatale, and armies, plus helper characters and civilians needing rescue— more and more characters to build more and more powerful conflicts between Bond and society.

复杂的电影有两个共同特征。首先是庞大的角色阵容。如果编剧将主角局限于社会冲突，那么正如广告所宣称的那样，他就需要“成千上万的演员”。詹姆斯·邦德不仅要面对强大的反派及其爪牙、刺客、蛇蝎美人、军队，还要面对协助他的角色和需要营救的平民——越来越多的角色构建出邦德与社会之间越来越激烈的冲突。

Second, a complicated film needs multiple sets and locations. If the writer progresses via physical conflict, he must keep changing the environment. A Bond film might start in a Viennese opera house, then go to the Himalayas, across the Sahara Desert, under the polar ice cap, up to the moon, and down to Broadway, giving Bond more and more opportunities for fascinating feats of derring-do.

其次，一部情节复杂的电影需要多个场景和地点。如果编剧通过肢体冲突推进剧情，就必须不断变换环境。一部邦德电影可能从维也纳歌剧院开始，然后前往喜马拉雅山脉，穿越撒哈拉沙漠，深入极地冰盖之下，登上月球，最后回到百老汇，让邦德有机会展现越来越多惊险刺激的冒险壮举。

Stories that are complicated only on the level of personal conflict are known as Soap Opera , an open-ended combination of Domestic Drama and Love Story in which every character in the story has an intimate relationship with every other character in the story—a multitude of family, friends, and lovers, all needing sets to house them: living rooms, bedrooms, offices, nightclubs, hospitals. Soap Opera characters have no inner or extra-personal conflicts. They suffer when they don’t get what they want, but because they’re either good people or bad, they rarely face true inner dilemmas. Society never intervenes in their air-conditioned worlds. If, for example, a murder should bring a detective, a representative of society, into the story, you can be certain that within a week this cop will have an intimate and personal relationship with every other character in the Soap.

那些仅在个人冲突层面上存在复杂情节的故事被称为肥皂剧，它是一种开放式的家庭剧和爱情故事的结合体，剧中的每个角色都与其他所有角色有着千丝万缕的联系——众多的家人、朋友和爱人，都需要特定的场景来容纳他们：客厅、卧室、办公室、夜总会、医院等等。肥皂剧中的人物没有内在或外在的冲突。当他们得不到想要的东西时，他们会感到痛苦，但由于他们非黑即白，很少面临真正的内心挣扎。社会从不干预他们如同空调房般的世界。例如，如果一起谋杀案让一位侦探——社会的代表——介入剧情，那么可以肯定的是，不出一个星期，这位警察就会与肥皂剧中的其他所有角色都建立起亲密的私人关系。

Stories that are complicated only on the level of inner conflict are not films, plays, or conventional novels. They’re prose works in the Stream of Consciousness genre, a verbalization of the inscape of thought and feeling. Again, a large cast. Even though we’re placed inside a single character, that character’s mind is populated with the memories and imaginings of everyone he has ever met or could hope to meet. What’s more, the density of imagery in the Stream of Consciousness work, such as NAKED LUNCH, is so intense that locations change, as it were, three or four times in a single sentence. A barrage of places and faces pours through the reader’s imagination, but these works are all on one, albeit richly subjective, level and, therefore, merely complicated.

那些仅在内心冲突层面上显得复杂的故事，并非电影、戏剧或传统小说。它们是意识流散文作品，是对内心思想和情感的语言化表达。同样，这类作品也涉及众多人物。尽管我们被置于单一角色的视角，但这个角色的脑海中却充斥着他曾经遇到或可能遇到的所有人的记忆和想象。此外，意识流作品（例如《裸体午餐》）中意象的密度极高，以至于在一句话中，场景就可能切换三四次。无数的地点和面孔涌入读者的想象，但这些作品都处于同一个层面——尽管主观性极强——因此，它们仅仅是复杂而已。

To achieve complexity the writer brings his characters into conflict on all three levels of life, often simultaneously. For example, the deceptively simple but complex writing of one of the most memorable events in any film for the last two decades: the French toast scene from KRAMER VS. KRAMER. This famous scene turns on a complex of three values: self-confidence, a child’s trust and esteem for his father, and domestic survival. As the scene begins, all three are at the positive charge.

为了营造复杂性，作者会让笔下的人物在生活的三个层面——通常是同时——陷入冲突。例如，《克莱默夫妇》中那段看似简单实则复杂的场景，堪称近二十年来电影史上最令人难忘的片段之一。这段著名的场景围绕着三个核心价值观展开：自信、孩子对父亲的信任和尊重，以及家庭的维系。场景开始时，这三个方面都处于积极的状态。

In the film’s first moments Kramer discovers his wife has left him and his son. He’s torn with an inner conflict that takes the form of doubts and fears that he’s in over his head versus a male arrogance telling him whatever women do is easy. As he opens the scene, however, he’s confident.

影片伊始，克莱默发现妻子离开了他和儿子。他内心充满矛盾，一方面怀疑自己是否能胜任，另一方面又带着一种男性的傲慢，认为女人做的事都轻而易举。然而，在影片的开场，他却显得信心满满。

Kramer has personal conflict. His son is hysterical, afraid he’ll starve without his mother to feed him. Kramer tries to calm his son, telling him not to worry, Mom will be back, but meantime it’ll be fun, like camping out. The child dries his eyes, trusting his father’s promises.

克莱默陷入了内心的挣扎。他的儿子歇斯底里地哭闹着，害怕没有妈妈喂饱他会饿死。克莱默试图安抚儿子，告诉他别担心，妈妈会回来的，而且在此期间也会很有趣，就像露营一样。孩子擦干眼泪，相信了父亲的承诺。

Finally, Kramer has extra-personal conflict. The kitchen is an alien world, but he strolls into it as if he were a French chef.

最后，克莱默还面临着一种超越个人层面的冲突。厨房对他来说是一个陌生的世界，但他却像个法国大厨一样轻松自如地走进去。

Perching his son on a stool, Kramer asks what he wants for breakfast and the kid says, “French toast.” Kramer takes a breath, pulls out a frying pan, pours in some grease, puts the pan on the stove, and turns the flame to high while he looks for ingredients. He knows French toast involves eggs, so he searches the refrigerator and finds some, but doesn’t know into what to break them. He rummages in the cupboard and comes down with a coffee mug that reads “Teddy.”

克莱默让儿子坐在凳子上，问他早餐想吃什么，孩子说：“法式吐司。”克莱默深吸一口气，拿出煎锅，倒了些油，把锅放在炉子上，开大火，一边找食材。他知道法式吐司要用到鸡蛋，于是翻遍冰箱，找到了一些，却不知道该用什么容器。他又在橱柜里翻找，最后拿出一个印着“泰迪”字样的咖啡杯。

The son sees the handwriting on the wall and warns Kramer that he’s seen his mother do this and she doesn’t use a mug. Kramer tells him it’ll work. He cracks the eggs. Some actually gets into the mug, the rest makes a gooey mess… and the child starts to cry.

儿子预感到不妙，警告克莱默说他见过妈妈这么做，她从来不用杯子。克莱默告诉他这招管用。他打碎了鸡蛋。一些蛋液确实流进了杯子里，剩下的则弄得黏糊糊的……孩子开始哭了起来。

The grease starts to spatter in the frying pan and Kramer panics. It doesn’t occur to him to turn off the gas; instead, he engages in a race against time. He bangs more eggs into the mug, rushes back to the refrigerator, grabs a quart of milk, and slops it up and over the brim of the mug. He finds a butter knife to break up the yolks, making an even gooier mess. The child can see he is not going to eat this morning and cries his eyes out. The grease is now smoking in the pan.

油开始在煎锅里飞溅，克莱默慌了。他竟然没想到要关掉煤气，反而开始争分夺秒。他往杯子里又打了几个鸡蛋，冲回冰箱，抓起一夸脱牛奶，一股脑儿地倒在杯子上，溢了出来。他又找到一把黄油刀，把蛋黄弄得更黏糊糊的。孩子意识到今天早上没饭吃了，嚎啕大哭。煎锅里的油已经开始冒烟了。

Kramer, desperate, angry, losing the fight to control his fears, grabs a slice of Wonder Bread, stares at it, and realizes it won’t fit in the mug. He folds it in half and stuffs it in, coming up with a dripping handful of soggy bread, yolk, and milk that he flings at the griddle, spattering and burning him and the child. He snatches the pan from the stove, scalding his hand, clutches his son’s arm, and pushes him through the door, saying, “We’ll go to a restaurant.”

克莱默绝望又愤怒，他再也无法控制自己的恐惧，抓起一片白面包，盯着它看了看，发现它放不进杯子里。他把面包对折塞进去，抓出一把湿漉漉的面包、蛋黄和牛奶，他一把抓起，扔向煎锅，溅得他和孩子都烫伤了。他一把抓起煎锅，烫伤了自己的手，抓住儿子的胳膊，把他推出门外，说：“我们去餐馆。”

Kramer’s male arrogance is overwhelmed by his fears, his self-confidence turning positive to negative. He’s humiliated in front of his frightened child, whose trust and esteem turn positive to negative. He’s defeated by a seemingly animated kitchen, as blow by blow, eggs, grease, bread, milk, and pan send him stumbling out the door, turning domestic survival from positive to negative.
